The events at Highrook went largely unreported by the Blacksands press. The High Council released little information concerning the investigation or its findings. But within a week, the order to condemn Ackeron Manor was issued by Mayor Aliston and civilians were barred from the vicinity of the house.
The investigators and their guilds were briefly lauded and then returned to their old lives, with new stories to tell and new ambitions to pursue.
The members of the Ackeron household that survived re-entered the city as quietly as they could, craving a time of rest and recuperation.

After the events at Highrook Atticus Hawke somehow found the money to build a grand house with a garden in Direwych.
But his newfound wealth did more than secure a good life for himself.
A year later he founded 'The New Dockland Fraternity', a labour union which pulled vagabonds out of criminality, and rescued the desperate from poverty.
Previously derided and demonised by the Blacksands establishment, Hawke soon became a prominent and famously oppositional member of the city elite.

Building upon the technical revelation she uncovered at Highrook, Mecanist Jane Astor became responsible for shepherding in a new era of ether-wave technologies.
Often seen as outlandish, or even dangerous, these technologies changed lives and founded new futures.
It was through Astor's promotion and propagation of this new science that Sophia Ackeron’s legacy was secured; new students in the decades to come would know her name, study her designs and learn her equations.

Inspired by Vitali’s writings in the years following the events at Highrook, a group of Blacksands academics banded together to study sleep and dreaming, eventually founding the 'Institute of the Subconscious Mind'.
Vitali, the honorary dean of this new school, slowly perfected the art of 'Tangible Dreaming' and began to sleep for longer and longer periods. In old age he woke and engaged with the world for just a few hours each day.
Those who knew him in those years remarked that the tempers of his youth had finally faded, and he always slept with a smile on his face.
The Institute of the Subconscious Mind

Six months after leaving Highrook Dr Alice Caligar discovered a cure for the Ash Plague, finally ridding herself and the city of its lingering shadow. Thereafter she became a prolific epidemiologist, developing cures for a wide range of terrible diseases.
The health of the whole realm was improved by her work, and even in old age she was said to have done more in each week of her work than other doctors achieved in a lifetime.
The Disease Archive she established before her death remained intact for generations, saving the lives of thousands, perhaps even millions, of people.

Before long, interest in the events at Highrook began to fade, and newspaper gossip turned to focus on other topics.
But, for unknown reasons, the order to demolish Ackeron Manor was never executed.
The shadowy form of Mr Tubbs still stalks the estate and the crumbling ruins of Highrook House peer down from the cliffs, like a dark bird watching over the city.

Amy was welcomed back to Blacksands by her extended family and Alfred's death was mourned by the locals, who smiled when remembering his clumsiness and compassion.
In time, she learned lacemaking from her aunties and joined a company in Verden Row. Here she found both financial independence and artistic recognition for her detailed yet often disturbing designs.
She is still visited by Atticus occasionally. His hulking figure is at odds with the filigree of the workshop, but his honest words are always welcome.

Lord Gideon Ackeron spent two years under house arrest at Senville Square.
He accepted his sentence with good grace and worked with both the High Council and Bleakhurst College to create a comprehensive report of the indicent at Highrook.
This process led to the arrest of several high ranking Seekers and the recovery of multiple stolen relics. After he was released, he remained with the college, continuing to document his experiences as a warning to any that might choose to follow.
He spent the rest of his life trying to repair the damage he had done.

Simon's affliction returned with him to Blacksands... But it did not kill him.
Eventually the curse faded. But the dark spiderweb traces it left upon his skin led him to adopt a reclusive lifestyle.
During his adolescence he remained withdrawn from society and in this isolation he became a prolific painter, producing many strange and otherworldly vistas.
His haunting canvases soon became sought after by museums and collectors. But however many dreams he drew, he could never rid himself of the nightmares that inspired them.

CARDS
Cards represent characters and objects you can interact with. Clicking on a card will give you more information about its potential uses. The main types of cards are as follows:
Character Cards: Display the status and attributes of a character (Needed to perform tasks).
Task Focus Cards: Items that can be used as the focus of a task (Needed to perform Tasks).
Task Support Cards: Items that add extra points to an attribute to help complete a task.
Information Cards: Items that present story fragments and hints.
Some cards have a glowing border. This means the card holds important story information and you are required to read it before continuing with your investigation.
The main use of cards is to perform Tasks in matching Rooms. Tasks are described in the following section.

CHARACTERS
In addition to investigating the mysteries of Highrook, you need to keep your team alive and well. Each character has a set of Skills (to help in tasks) and four Vital Statistics that define their health and state of mind.
Injury: This represents how hurt a character is. If it reaches 100%, the character will be incapacitated and unable to perform any task except to recover their health.
Fatigue: This increases with each task performed. When characters become excessively tired, they might begin to fail at the tasks they are given.
Hunger: Characters get hungry over time. If left unfed, they will eventually suffer injury from starvation.
Madness: Characters lose sanity when facing horrors or performing certain tasks. High levels of madness cause characters to behave erratically.
You can treat these negative conditions by sleeping in the Guest Rooms or consuming food and medicine in the Dining Room. You can also change how much impact these stats have in the game options menu.

THE GAME BOARD
The game board shows the various rooms in the manor where you can conduct your investigations. Some locations will be unavailable when the game begins and it is your job to work out how to access them.
You can get information about a Room by selecting its title bar, or any of the squares that make up the room itself. This will show you a description of the room and its associated attributes.
You can zoom in and out of the board with the mouse wheel (or keys q and e), and pan around by holding down the right mouse button (or keys w,a,s,d).
All rooms (and cards) have Attributes listed in their descriptions;etc. The attribute associated with a room indicates which cards can be used there.
For example the (Devices) attribute is present on both the Study Code card and the Machine Room, meaning you can use the code in that location.
Placing items and characters in matching rooms allows you to perform Tasks. Executing tasks is how you uncover new items and progress in the game.

INTRODUCTION
Welcome to The Horror at Highrook, a card-crafting cosmic horror boardgame! You control a team of investigators, sent to examine the disappearance of a noble family from their ancestral home.
To progress through the game you must combine characters and items in order to complete tasks across the ancient estate. Experiment and explore, there are many mysteries to unravel. If you reach a dead end, turn your attention elsewhere for a while and try something else.
A small set of Introductory Tasks are listed to the bottom left, to help you get started.
You can close this window now, and work things out as you play.
Or you can read the other sections in this guide to learn more about the game systems. This information is always accessible from the in-game menu [Esc] so you can return to it at any time.

TASKS
Each room contains a localTask square. If you place a Task Focus Card in the square (with an attribute that matches the room) the Inspector panel will show information about the task, and the attribute level needed to perform it.
Room tasks always require a Character card to be present in the local Character square. This character can contribute their own attribute levels to the task. For example, Scholar Vitali could contribute +1 to the task of deciphering a notebook.
Harder tasks require higher levels of an attribute. You can place additional Support cards into the room (in any square) to help you meet the challenge. For example, adding 'Palatinos Pen' might add another +1 to the total.
Once the attribute requirements are met you can then execute the task. If a task produces a card, but the task room is full, the new card will be placed into the Temporary Storage area.
If the task fails with the phrase "Perhaps we should focus our efforts elsewhere for a while" it means that ALL the result cards are already on the board. But if you use a support card from the results (Charcoal for example) it will be available to appear from the task again.

TIMERS
At the top-right of the screen is a Sundial, this displays the current in-game time and the number of days you have been in the manor. You can use the buttons beneath the sundial to control the speed of the game (keyboard- 1,2,3). You can also pause/unpause the game at any time (keyboard- space bar).
All tasks take a specific amount of time to perform and certain game-events are also triggered by the passage of time. Don't be afraid to pause frequently, especially if you want to read everything!
Beneath the sundial is a button to access the Records panel, a storage space for information cards. You can send information cards to the records panel by right clicking to bring up a context menu, or by using the button in the inspector.
Storing cards can help to keep the board less cluttered and you can always read them later.

Dear Investigators,
By order of the High Council you are granted license to commandeer Highrook Manor and its associated facilities.
You have been commissioned to investigate the disappearance of the Ackeron family - the owners of the estate - who were reported missing several days ago.
The Ackerons were well known in the city, and their vanishing is concerning - especially considering a rumoured affiliation with the Seeker's Communion.
Please treat any evidence you might find as confidential and report immediately to the council when your task is complete.
A news report is included to provide further context on this unusual event.
Lord Mayor Aliston

Dear Sophia
It took me some time, but I finally had a look over your designs.
The underlying frameworks seem sound. However, I am not sure that an Aeroplex coil is quite the right thing to stabilise the resistances in your first blueprint. Your use of valve inserters in the second is quite unorthodox!
I began to make some alterations to both schematics but after some consideration I realised that my edits were likely to introduce anomalies and undermine the work.
I reverted the changes and think you should proceed with your original designs, I look forward to hearing the results.
Good luck, dear friend!
P.

Dear Sophia
I finally found the schematic for that thermostatic valve you were asking about. It was stuffed behind Henry's desk. Heaven knows how the man is so untidy!
I was troubled to hear that Gideon is behaving strangely. After you told me of his manner, I spoke to the staff at Wilkins and they told me he hadn't been in for weeks - and when he was last present he was locked in a muffled argument with some folk from Senville and Deep Spire.
When they left, rumours sprung up that they were part of the Communion. But the folk at Wilkins love to gossip, so I don't know how much truth there was in it... Anyway take care my dear, and I hope to see you at the Candlemass lectures.
P.

A VANISHING AT HIGHROOK
The Ackeron family, one of the city's most eligible houses, has disappeared under suspicious circumstances this week.
A delivery boy from Direwych Market is reported to have discovered the family's absence when he arrived at their clifftop manor to deliver tinned fish. The boy, who has subsequently been treated for delirium, is reported to have spoken about seeing the place as if struck by a storm.
The Ackeron family were not immediately found by a local tollsman, and their servants - a maid and an estate warden - also seem to have been missing for some time. The High Council announced that it has commissioned a cross-guild team to investigate this disturbing occurrence of vanishment.

BLACKSANDS RESIDENTS DREAM SAME DREAM
In what is being described as a bout of mass hysteria by sleep clinicians, many Blacksands residents have reported having the same dream on Tuesday night.
The occurrence, which has been dismissed by the mayor, who claims to have had a 'very different' dream that night, saw people reporting night-time visions of a long hall in which a 'nasty sort of shadow' produced feelings of 'dread and sickly loathing'.
The High Council has appealed for calm, and suggested women and children drink one milk cup of egg-brandy before sleep to treat any unsettling night-time visions.

'INEXPLICABLE' UNCLAIMED IMPORTS SEIZED, AUCTIONED OFF
Blacksands' port tariff agents have seized the contents of a warehouse for which no dock receipt could be produced. The imports, whose anonymous buyer failed to collect this week, were revealed to contain a series of mechanical parts and 'etched plates' for which no immediate use could be determined by the agents.
'If the buyer, initials S.A., wishes to reclaim their property then they will have to bid for them at the public auction like anyone else,' docking agent Parlour Eustice told the Gazette.
'And then they will have to explain why these imports were improperly registered in the first place,' said Eustice.

SICK CLOWN DISTURBS LIBRARY TOAD SPEAKER
A public lecture at Blacksands General library by noted toad expert, Dr Thylen Mortottle, was disturbed on Wednesday by the actions of a 'fully painted' clown.
The entertainer, who was noted to have been from 'out of town', unnerved lecture attendees by standing silently in the audience for the first part of the lecture. He was later ejected on issuing 'toad-like screams' as Dr Mortottle's speech continued. The clown, whose whereabouts are unknown, is said to have made threats, and brandished a 'bone knife' at librarians.
Dr Mortottle has reportedly cancelled forthcoming events in his pond-life lecture series.

EARTH TREMORS SHAKE REGION - DAMAGE TO BLACKSANDS TENEMENT DETERMINES DEMOLISHMENT.
A shifting of the Earth has been reported in all areas of the Blacksands locality this week, with damage to some buildings. A tenement in the Direwych area has been condemned as a result of the tremors, with the mayor announcing that it is to be taken down within two weeks.
Affected families are to be housed at the Hocklin Mill, which has also suffered minor damage from the quaking.
It is understood that such events are naturally occurring, albeit rare, palpitations of the deep stones of the Earth.

INTENSE SMOG CAUSES CHOKING EPIDEMIC
A mixture of woodsmoke, coal fumes, and naturally-occurring sea mist has combined to inflict a terrible plight upon Blacksands, with widespread bad-breathing and choking reported.
The mayor has asked people to stay in their homes, and to only venture out with breathing apparatus or fine-weave masks to stave off the worst of the hazard. The conditions are expected to lift when the weather brings fresh sea air into the region.
If you are choking, you are advised to drink strongly salted hot water and convalesce in bed.

A ghostly vision of Gideon appears. In the blurring of the worlds it is neither here nor there.

Cyclopean spires pierce the blood red sky. Bird-things that are little more than rags flounder and scream across the cracked desert ground.

I am rooted to the putrid earth. The tendrils climb up me like vicious insects. They close around my limbs, wrapping around me, a swaddle of thorny straps.
I feel them tighten, slowly crushing the life from my frozen form. A host of distorted figures stands witness, each one malformed in its own abhorrent way.
There are no more revelations to drain from the depths of this cup.

I am worried about the master. Since he started talking with those Seekers the house has been filling up with all kinds of oddments. Horrible antiques and tattered books full of foreign writing. Dire portraits I would not look upon.
Amy says that just touching some of these items made Simon poorly. And now the Lord himself is suffering from some sort of melancholy!
Perhaps Lady Sophia is worried too, she asked me to bring some of her stuff down to the cellars. Told me that she might start working down here.
I am thinking that if anyone else gets ill, I might have to start 'misplacing' some of these weird objects when I handle the deliveries... I don't like to deceive, but I don't want Amy getting poorly either.

Things are getting worse with the Master. I heard strange noises in the Chapel last night and went to investigate.
Lord Ackeron was there, in a circle of candlelight, a book in one hand and some old necklace thing in the other.
He was jabbering and incanting - 'breach the circles', 'coalesce and condense', 'meld the mind and join the flesh'. Horrible!
Now I am even more worried for him and the family. I do not want anyone else getting poorly.
The master has been getting even more deliveries of Seeker materials, too. Ingots stamped with old time runes. I am no thief, but I will turn to hiding these when they arrive.
I hope if someone one day judges me, they will understand why I have done what I done.

Perhaps I am cursed. Since I have been 'diverting' the Lords deliveries my dreams have been most strange. I see them like vivid plays upon a stage. Visions!
I see a lady - a right pretty lady - she is outside the house, just sitting solitary in the courtyard.
The 'Song' is her name. I just know it, in the dream. She looks like a chanteuse from Wilkins or another fancy city place. But there's something about her eyes. And her dress. It shifts around like water.
Last night I saw her 'You are saving them' she told me. I tried to speak but I could not. Perhaps I cannot speak in dreams.
'Bring our words back to us' she then says 'and the world will be set right again'
I want to get closer to her! To know what it means. But damn Tubbs woke me up jumping on my face.

I have spread the metal runes around the house in hiding places. Amy caught me moving one, but I do not think she saw what I was doing.
I am not sure what I did has helped the curse though. Simon has not returned from Blacksands, Sophia seems to have vanished and the Lord is still down there, chanting.
My own dreams are also becoming more like nightmares.
The Song was in my dream again. She stood on our own clifftops, her eyes shining out bright, like the moon. She sung for the darkness. She wants me to bring her the runes! Then she can cure Lord Gideon's madness, she can protect us, shelter us. She said. In the dream.
I have started to hear her voice... in the day. I am afraid of what might happen.

I was looking for musical recordings for the boy to play. He loves the magic of sound coming from that clunky old machine he has in his room.
I promised him I would bring him anything I could find and I have got him some good ones. Music, stories and the like. I found one in the archives the other day that I will not let him hear.
It was right far in the stacks. 'Voltok' or something it says on the label. Excited, I took it to Simon's room, but he wasn't there. I thought to give it a listen myself.
Well, I wish I had not. Such evil words were on the thing. I would call it a choir of witches! I took the wretched thing and put it up in the eaves in our chambers, so that no one ever again has to listen to that foul noise.

Pa Alfred is up to something. I don't know if it is down to his bad dreams. He's been talking in his sleep, fever-like. I keep hearing him muttering, even crying.
Worse, though, I know he has been stashing deliveries around the house. They're things addressed to his lordship. Hidden by Pa Alfred.
I do not ask him about it. He is troubled enough, what with Lord Gideon acting all strange, and Simon getting so poorly. We are a sad household.
I don't want Pa to get into trouble when the things he hid are missed. I have made notes of them.
He thinks I don't know, but he is about as subtle as a goat and his eyes are so bad he can hardly see me when I am presently standing in front of him.

I found one of the things Pa Alfred has been hiding. It's in the box with this note. An odd metal block, with old writing stamped in it.
I don't want him to know I found it, and I don't want us to have anything to do with it. The writing on it is all old and smoothed out, but it gives me the shivers.
I am going to put it in the well in this box so that we can forget it was ever here.
Maybe Pa Alfred will forget about it. I hope so, he is getting very vague recently. He keeps going on weird late night walks, mumbling to himself and peering around, as if he is looking for someone.

I do not know what I should do. Pa Alfred went off towards the cliffs tonight, perhaps to hide another of these deliveries that should be given to Lord Ackeron. He has not come back.
The mists are thick now. They come up from the sea and they are like a blinding veil! What if he has stumbled? What if he has fallen? Pa is just an old man. I should go and look for him, but I am not allowed to roam the cliffs on my own. There is no one here to help me.

I was hoping to find more evidence of Sophia's fate. It has been years since we last spoke but I cannot forget her soft voice and sharp mind.
Sophia was... is... a natural scientist, hamstrung by a social code that smothers her skill and ambition.
I loathed her husband. He was egotistical and pompous, but also distracted, which boded well for our 'friendship'. Our trysts began as innocent conversations buoyed by an enthusiasm that I first thought was platonic and later realised was more.
Perhaps we can still find her, I truly hope so. I must work to ensure that people come to know the talent that woman had and what she might have become if given the freedom to pursue her dreams. Just in case the worst does happen.

The other investigators each seem to have their own thoughts and intentions here. True, we are working together intensely and competently to solve this terrible mystery, but I cannot help but feel the notions and contrivances going on behind each of their eyes.
It matters not, I have my own reasons for needing to spend time exploring this place. Let Vitali indulge his obsessions and Atticus break things. I will contribute to the mission in my own ways, to protect Sophia, her family, and her legacy. Little else matters.

My mind now turns to what might happen when we escape this place. It has already been awful enough that I can be certain none of us will leave here unscarred and unchanged. What a curse has been wrought, and what foolishness.
When I find myself recovered, I shall make it a task to decry unnatural curiosities and to castigate the meddlers like Vitali and Gideon.
In truth it is only the mecanists who really understand how life should be approached. Not without feeling, but certainly with reason and caution. Only human invention can preserve us and our world. All else is indulgent folly.

What is Atticus doing, creeping about in the corners of dark corridors, late at night? I cross paths with him, but he does not speak, just grunts and moves on.
And what of Caligar? She seems never to remove that mask, and it begins to stir thoughts in me that I have suppressed; what does she really want here? Why does seem so interested in where things might be hidden or buried?
The longer we spend here the more I realise that everyone, and not just Vitali, has some special and unhealthy interest in this place beyond the mission we've been charged with.
It worries me. If we are all looking to other ambitions what will become of the Ackerons themselves, the focus of this whole investigation?

Do not normally do writing. But something is off. This Highrook place is a wreck. Full of junk and books. Broken things. Don't like it. Smells wrong. Feels wrong.
The Scholar is a brain-worm and Astor is boring. A puppet-loving mecanist. The doc is the only normal one. Wish she would take that mask off.
She fixed me up last spring for the Keel Fever. She cared nowt about the bodies. Waded all in and treated us. In some fancy skirts, too. Elegant you might say. Even in all that filth.
Anyways, Joskel asked me to get his silver snuff box back from the cellars here - apparently he dropped it last summer when helping with a delivery. If I leave it by the gate in the courtyard one of his boys will pick it up. -A

Plenty of opportunity to make extra coin here. But beginning to wonder if I will ever get to spend it.
It's good that Vitali can read the Ackeron's weird books, but he's still a meddler. There is a limit to what people should meddle with. Vitali is one of those that cannot help but meddle.
Perhaps it will help us here, but honest, I would rather have something more solid to grasp. Mumbo-jumbo is slippery as an eel.
If I get home from this wretched heap then I will start planning for my life. I cannot end up like my father or grandfather. I intend to live out my old man days in style. If I'm lucky maybe I can come back from here with more than just my fee. -A

Something about this place has me putting words down. I am not one for writing. But sometimes I do it just to prove to people that I can! I have my book learning. I just know that it has its place.
Anyways, Caligar seemed impressed to find me writing. She said it was 'indicative of a private mind', whatever that means. She is the only one here I would really trust in a pinch. She's got what it takes. And it will come to a pinch. No doubt.
My family always said that we had no business with doctors. Said that was all just snake oil. But I don't think Caligar is a faker. She is a smart one for sure, but not all high and mighty like the other two. A private mind! -A

The Doctor has done so much for us here. The others don't see it. But I do. We might even be dead without her.
I know my own work to keep them all fed and protected from the elements helps, too. But there are skills which are beyond me. Skills that we all need in this hellhole.
I wonder if I will still write notes like this once I get out of this place? This experience will leave me a changed man. For certain. I was never much of a thinker. But it's hard not to brood in this place. And hard not to think about how life might have been different.
I will lead a better life one day. And stop having to sell my muscle for jobs like this. But who will live that life with me? -A

Dear Dr Caligar Astor. We were pleased to receive your correspondence. We of course offer all the support we can to our members in difficult situations. It is important to understand, however, that a situation like the one you have found yourself in was entered into deliberately. You have placed yourself in jeopardy in a way that puts you outside mandatory responsibilities of the board, and as such we expect you will understand the limitations on our ability to interfere.
We trust that you remain steadfast, healthy, rational, and of sound mind for our summer conference. - Caincross Surgeons Board

I have only been here a few days, but this place is already beginning to get under my skin. It doesn't help that I can't access my own 'medicine' here.
I need to find some organic evidence of the family if am to be able to properly employ my skills.
But, as always, the discovery of a body would be a double edged event; the intrigue of an organic trail paired with the grief of yet another death. And I have seen too much death in my work already! It is why I blunt the sharpness of the world with drink.
On another note, it seems that I have met the hireling, Atticus, before. I do remember the incident at Aldwerth and his hulking presence. He is a crude man, but an impressive physical specimen.

There is a mood in this place that is as infectious as any disease. It settles upon the mind and you find yourself losing minutes, hours, even days, to introspection. Perhaps it is because we are all so distracted. We are seldom in the same space, each of us researching our own avenue of the awfulness of this place.
I cannot imagine how a hulk like Atticus is processing what is happening here. Astor and Vitali both have sharp minds, and a rational education. But Atticus has only the education of a simple, difficult life.
Yet there is a tenderness. A habit of care. He brings us what he has trapped or foraged out on the cliffs in a way that indicates duty, but also suggests a hidden compassion and humanity.

I have always been concerned with diseases of the body, but what we see here makes me wonder if the true malady is one of the world. Just as a sickness is a derangement of the systems of the body by the introduction of some alien antagonist, so our own world is sickened by the presence of things to which it must respond and react.
Perhaps, when all this is done, we should look at what might make our world more resistant to corruption? If a person must eat well, see the sun shine, and keep themselves active, then there are also habits that the world as a whole must adopt to protect from decay? A philosophy for defence of our realm.
Indeed, I must strive to remove my own poison from my life and habits.

It is only my training and experiences as a doctor that have allowed me to survive in this place. The others endure also, in their own ways. Education and experience are the tuning which makes a person survive.
This is even true of Atticus. He might be a simple beast with limited pleasures, but I have seen him write, and I know he thinks more than his exterior might suggest. I doubt I will see him again after all this is done, but if I do I will not be uncomfortable with such a meeting.

The Circles demarcate realms of being. In a sense, our own world is a Circle, too, albeit one far outside the direct influence of that other place. To exist under a particular Circle's influence is to inhabit a particular set of rules which that Circle calls reality.
Entities native to a Circle cause chaos when they move between realms. They ignite a clash of realities. Such transportations bring aspects of the domains they are defined by with them. Like backgammon pieces appearing on a chess board.
Percival Miller

The Circles or Rings of Nibiru are complete within themselves. An ouroboros of existence, cycling dimensional material in infinite loops.
As these loops formed, they must have become separated from the other planes of being. They began to exist 'alongside' our more conventional realities.
Although uncoupled from us, the nested rings can still cast disturbances into our world - like ripples on a pond, or light scattered by crystals.
Percival Miller

Like our own solar system, each circle or loop of Nibiru is the orbit of some strange land. Biomes of uncanny design, host to their own strange fauna and flora.
But as with recent atomic revelations, the length of a loop is not merely its circumference. The rings contain an unknown distance, traversing a full winding of a loop leads not back to the beginning but forward into another uncanny circuit.
Percival Miller

As the watcher disintegrates, whispers float in from the past.
Upon this hill, this sacred hill, shall I become a pile of bones. For we shall build a dwelling! And therein shall we abide.
The call of a gull echoes across the distance of time.
Be not in sorrow, my kin. This desolate place shall engage us in solitude, and there shall be a feast, and the old ones will see the fire, and they shall rejoice. Thus spake the first master of Highrook!

As the watcher disintegrates, whispers float in from the past.
The plague has taken our lord. Now, he is gone. To the land of the dead. Which now lies close at hand. Indeed, the same souls that walk in that shadowed place walk with us here, in these halls. This great house shall not serve another generation, and it shall pass into ruin. As all things must.
Come, you who can walk still, the raiders are in the fields! We must take up with axe and lantern. There is nothing more to be done.

As the watcher disintegrates, whispers float in from the past.
And I wrote to mother and explained that I had purchased this simply exquisite ruin atop the cliffs. I shall live in the shattered tower and write my sonnets. 'Verily, unto the horizon I do see...' well, I do not claim to be some gilded bard.
We cannot all expect to have our voice echo down the ages. If the best I can do is a tome of my poems in the archive of some great family, then so be it. The romance of this place should see to that!

As the watcher disintegrates, whispers float in from the past.
They say, Your Worship, that there were sacred stones in this place even before the first settlers built their 'dark fort'. Indeed, there are signs of settlement from before people are recorded to have lived in these lands. Ha, no, I don't know who could have raised the stones. Gods? Giants!
No, no. History is but a silly game. The new house we are building here is about the future - burying the bones of that past.

As the watcher disintegrates, whispers float in from the past.
Those within the house cannot know we are here, brothers. Our action is as secret as it is sacred. For this is the place where the boundary wears very thin. Indeed, I know that even now your shining souls press against it, yearning for the other place. Here the wall will prove too fragile to contain us.
Hush! We move in silence, so none shall detect our passing. So it shall be; steadfast, and relentless.

As the watcher disintegrates, whispers float in from the past.
Yes, yes! Sell to this Voltok woman. Do it quickly! We cannot stand another season in this wretched place. First my sister, then my children! Why did they go down there? Oh, those caves. Each one a terrible mouth.
Why is this place so hungry? I tell you it is a vampire, drinking the blood of the people who dwell within it. Henry! Sell the damned house! It is a curse! A doom! Even now we sicken! Oh my, look at your teeth. Henry, your teeth. Those were the last ones...

Dear Brothers,
I have finally obtained the ceremonial goblet of Irma Voltok. As you know, we have been in search of this item ever since our interest in Highrook began. Irma was a previous owner of the estate. She was a much-lauded poet, praised for her vivid and otherworldly compositions.
Although it is unclear how much true insight Voltok displayed in her work, it is evident that she used the relic (along with various chemical concoctions) to summon visions of Nibiru.
As such it was seen as important to obtain the goblet as soon as possible and add it to our inventory.
Communion Provisioner H.

The 'Brain Cap' I bought from Direwych appears to be a waste of time. I hoped it would aid Simon's classes. However the gadget not only requires the support of the machine room, it also seems to operate entirely randomly! Instead of focusing the users mind for study, it imparts all kinds of chaotic visions.
I was tempted to return it, but Gideon disagrees. I think partly because he wishes to avoid leaving the house! I am concerned that his solitude is a sign of something more troubling.
I have been so immersed in my own studies recently, that I did not notice this change in him. Maybe it has something to do with his work for the Seekers Communion? I will have to ask him when the opportunity presents itself.

Its has been some time since the weather has permitted me to continue my experiments outside. The smog-laden rain chokes up my devices with an oily film.
Today however, a break in the clouds has given me the opportunity to accomplish at least a little work. I left Simon with Amy. He is still ill, but my husband says not to worry, a cold is doing the rounds.
I am still waiting for a delivery of schematics from the town, but I will test my prototype today, until either the sun-light or my power supply fail. I need more data to improve my design.
Typical! A rainstorm began at noon and I had to retreat. The generator I bought from Direwych might be ruined. I'm going to try and dry it out, but I suspect that will not help. I hate this blasted climate!

The direction of Gideon's new work unsettles me. He is obsessed with a mythical place called Nibiru. He seems convinced it truly exists, populated with wondrous treasures and powerful entities.
I pray that this new obsession has not involved Simon - especially considering his recent illness. He idolizes his father and is always eager to help.
Of course, I blame the Seekers for Gideon's transformation, I am sure they are exploiting him for their own gain. He even suggested that I should halt my development of the field phone and instead aid him and the Communion.
Perhaps I am being paranoid, but I am going to make my work more secure. The last thing I want is for my research to end up in the hands of some cultists.

The unsettling changes in my husband's character are accelerating. He acts like he is a Seeker now, spouting their twisted occult adages, and pouring over their dusty tomes. I fear I am losing him to their fanaticism.
His mania also seems to have overridden any concern for Simon's illness. He ignored the Caincross Yard medicals who came to help and instead spent the time placing the house in lockdown! He is constantly distracted, and refuses to talk about Simon at all.
I am not sure what his intentions are, but I have begun to keep my work in the cellar atrium in order to avoid any potential clashes.
I will place a spare key with this note so I cannot get locked out of there too!

Simon is gone... Gideon refuses to tell me where he is, only that he is safe and protected from whatever illness was plaguing him. I think he has sent my son to the Seekers, to one of their secret hideouts...
I am so angry that I am shaking as I write... Gideon is deluded! As if dangerous arcane rituals can help, where medicine cannot! He needs familiar faces and proper treatment, not strangers experimenting with his health.
I cannot continue my work until I have found where Gideon has sent my son! I will store my materials in the cellars until I have located him.
Once he is back I will make plans for the two of us to leave, even if temporarily, we cannot stay here safely any longer.

A horrible truth has been unveiled... Simon, my dear son... is not with the Seekers, or anywhere in Blacksands... he has been sent somewhere... else...
I heard Gideon talking in the Chapel last night. He was conversing with someone, with something... a voice as cold as the night sky, a guttural alien tongue.
The visitor claimed that Simon was 'In the arms of Nibiru' - that foul place my husband is so obsessed with. They continued, describing the door to this place as both 'below and beyond' the house.
I stood there outside the room, incensed with rage.
There is no use confronting my husband about this anymore - I fear for what he might do. I need to access this 'Nibiru' myself, and rescue my son.

I am sure that the path to saving Simon lies somewhere beneath the house. I heard Gideon talk to the stranger about 'a door below' and much of his occult library was unearthed from the depths of the cellars... so it seems like the best place to look.
At the lowest levels of the cellars are odd tunnels, where the dark red brick gives way to stone and rock, twisting further into the earth.
I have already found evidence of activity in these passages, footprints, pipe ash and some locked doors I know nothing about.
I will move to quarters in Blacksands for a few days to prepare my equipment. And then I will return and attempt to track Gideon's path further into the tunnels.

To whoever finds this note...
Do not follow my path, you will not find us... They have their threads in us, all of us. They pull and we cannot resist. If you seek us out, you too will be lost...
If I can, and before its too late, I will close the doors... I will shatter the gates... and scatter the fragments... and I beseech you,
Do Not Follow!
I have made such errors of judgement... such acts of vanity and greed... and for what?

I have gathered most of the tablets I need to compose the rite. And yet I am hesitant. I must act quickly if I am to rescue my son, but I feel unprepared, and certain items from my occult armoury have... gone missing. I may have misplaced them in my confusion, but it is more likely that they have been taken by Sophia. Perhaps even one of the servants!
Alfred has been avoiding my gaze for weeks and Amy is quiet as a mouse. They suspect something. And I in turn must suspect them. I will search their rooms and confront them if I find evidence of larceny.
Is it rash to step further into Nibiru without all my tools? I am wary, but the Burning Moon still calls to me in my dreams, and only my ascendency can guarantee my poor son's safety!

Sophia has left me. I am now sure she has fled to Blacksands. Our last few conversations were terrible, rage-filled exchanges. I expect she is in town now, rallying her colleagues for support. It is probably best... It is certainly not safe for her to stay here right now.
It is clear to me now that the Rites of the Circles require words drawn not just from books or tablets, but from relics taken from the domain of Nibiru itself.
This also means that I can no longer rely on the Seekers for every scrap of knowledge and I must begin to forge my own path and acquire more relics of incantation.
Perhaps I can assemble a new rite from the Atlaxian cartouches I am gathering. Their origin might be the domain of Nibiru itself.

I am to cross over tonight. I cannot wait for the Seekers' assistance, they are too slow and weak. My family is in danger.
I have found a hidden path. One that lay within the moon mirror. It was here all along. My predecessor, Irma Voltok, had locked it in the archives, not knowing its true use.
I summoned my reflection with the relic. A dark and crooked doppelganger. He gifted me the words to follow the secret path.
But then he would not leave! Even as his form faded, he attacked me. Words and fists and teeth and screaming!
I fled and returned the mirror to its container. I do not need it now, I know the secret way. I will cross over tonight... I must put right what I have wrought. I shall redeem my folly.

The Dreamleaf potions are working! I took another one last night at bedtime... And in my slumber I saw it! A relic of Valhasa, a glowing shard of light. An ancient pendant, buried in a deep chamber of the undercoves, just as the Seekers said.
I sent Simon down to find it. My old eyes are worse than his and he loves to explore the caves. He is nimble and the ichtis sleep even lower than the Seekers' caves, so i knew he would be safe. Following the outline of my dream, he found the pendant, returning it proudly to me, his eyes bright with excitement.
I hope one day to show him the wonders he helped bring forth... But for now, just a few more fragments and I can complete the first steps of my journey.

I have the Valhasa Tear and the fragments to accompany it... but at what cost?
My son brought more than just the relic back from the depths. He is afflicted with some unearthly wasting disease. The doctors from Caincross could not help him, and he is now so frail that I fear he may not recover on his own.
I hope to find some assistance for him via my work, or from the Seekers. Perhaps the cure lies somewhere within the walls of Nibiru.
In the meantime, I am sealing the Chapel, just as I have closed the Laboratory. I don't want anyone else to stumble across my work and end up injured...

Simon's illness is worsening... The Communion tells me that the only cure lies in pressing onwards. But I have already unleashed things I never wanted to see.
This morning the spawn of the First Circle came again, writhing putrid grubs, spilling out of the cracks in the boards. I do not know how to appease them, and I am so tired. Things are becoming... untethered.
In my fatigue, I have mislaid the Valhasa Tear, or it has mislaid itself.
I must begin hiding the tools and ritual fragments... I cannot have my family fall prey to their effects again.

I cannot find my tools anymore...
It's as if the house is shifting around me. Scraps and relics wandering from room to room... I am so weary with study and drained from ritual that I cannot think straight.
I am attempting to keep track of the fragments, and I know I could acquire replacements if need be, but I fear I am stumbling into the darkness without the protections I need.
The communion is urging me on, offering support from afar. But they are not subject to the nightmares that I see in every shadow.

I heard the hounds again last night. I could not decide if their howling was real, or just echoes in my own mind.
I have barely slept. Simon's condition is worsening.
I must find a solution either in words or actions... The eye will not close again! I must find a way to blind it while I seek the cure...
I can still see the Key in my dreams. Her bifurcated head, that dark gaping maw....
But No! I am a Seeker now, even without the ceremony. I will step beyond the threshold, I will compel the instruments of Nibiru to obey me.

He was dying... I had no choice... I summoned the Key while the veils were still thin... and I demanded that she take him into the gardens of the First Circle.
The rot will stop there. He will not worsen... But he cannot stay long without protection. He will become ash... he will wither away.
I will raise myself further. I can enter Nibiru of my own volition. I will compel the Needle to cure Simon. I will bring him home.
Sophia must not know! It is best she believes that I have sent him to some private city infirmary. Once I have returned she will see the reasoning and the glorious path ahead for all of us.
The shadow is cast long across this house... but perhaps there is still time?

I think Sophia has been hiding her work from me. She used to share her discoveries, but I know she harbours a mistrust of the Communion, and ever since my collaboration with them she has become withdrawn.
Admittedly I have been pre-occupied myself. My work is now beyond the realms of mundane science, but I know she will not discuss the new paths that I have been taking - she considers them 'unsafe'.
Yesterday I found a fragment of some mecanist blueprint in the School Room, a part of her field phone design. But now is not the time to introduce any anomalies to the local spectra. It would disturb my work.
I will seal the fragment away, and perhaps discuss it with her when my work with the Seekers is done.

I... the circles are drawing in, I am not sure if I am outside or inside. I hear the sea of stars lapping on the shores of Nibiru. In my dreams, I feel the oily roots of the First Circle grasping at my flesh. And when I awake part of me is still there, within those obsidian spires.
I will not let my mind be drowned by these outer beings! I am a Seeker; I opened the gate... I made the Key shelter my son... I will find a path to ascension.
I know I can find the strength to succeed. Another of the entities had crossed over yesterday, a gross maggot of disturbing proportions. I destroyed it before anyone else saw, and was rewarded with such a sense of triumph. I will protect my family.
Sophia will understand soon. But for now I must hide the truth from her - she has been spying on me, I know it..

I need to shake off this childish apprehension and press forward. But I am vexed. Despite searching the entire estate and exhausting my contacts, I don't have enough fragments to complete the rite.
The Communion has offered to meet me in the Labyrinthine Chapel. They are to re-consecrate the place, and its position beneath the estate makes it a powerful locus for rituals.
I have already scoured the halls below in pursuit of my own research, but perhaps the Seekers' return will reveal some things that I had overlooked?
In truth, I think that they had underestimated my skill and are now attempting recompense. Nibiru is whispering to me. I can feel its power growing inside me... If I can contain and control it, then the Seekers will soon need me more than I need them!

New Pilgrims at Highrook? A re-opening is at hand, but you do not appear to be Seekers. I pray you have the insight to act wisely, where Gideon acted without real consideration.
Ackeron was a talented scholar, but his downfall was to trust the Communion. Their knowledge and ambitions are flawed and naive.
His use of Dreamleaf led to his discovery of the Tear, but his subsequent actions were rash and ill-informed. I hope that your progress will be more enlightened.
To this end, I offer you a part of the whole you seek. Make good use of this gift and we might speak again.
V

Dear Gideon,
Your efforts have been noticed. You are new to the Communion, yet we already sense great potential in your practice.
As discussed, we will aid you in your work and provide such guidance as we can. In return you must follow that guidance, and pledge yourself to our order.
As you are aware, Highrook rests above the Blacksands Undercoves, a network of subterranean smuggling routes and hidden chambers. An old Seekers' sanctuary still lies within those caves.
Descend and locate this shrine if you can. We believe objects of great power still remain there, hidden in that gloom.
The Communion

Dear Gideon,
The fragments of lore you are compiling are symbolic shards, scraps of shattered knowledge. They may seem incomprehensible in isolation, but gather them all and absorb their lessons. Only then, when you assemble the whole, will a new rite will be formed.
The Opening Eye, The Ashen Hammer, The Fallen Sky, The Broken Spear. Each incantation opens the mind to deeper power and knowledge.
Persist brother, you are close to communing with the first circle of Nibiru. Once the eye has been opened you will truly begin to see the glory that awaits.
The Communion

Brother Ackeron.
We understand that in recovering the Tear your son has been hurt. It is unfortunate and regrettable, but do not swerve from your path now. The knowledge and power you will acquire can cleanse your son of any ailment, voidborne or otherwise.
You must reach further, into the inner circles of The Unseen Twin. Only there will you find the power to heal your son and fortify your family for what is to come.
Prepare your summoning chamber, assemble the rite of the Opening Eye and speak with The Key, the guardian of the First Circle. You must pass through the darkness to reach the illumination beyond.
The Communion

Brother Ackeron.
Your skills improve. However, your recent divergence from our instructions is concerning.
We know that you acted in order to protect your son from further illness, but the instruments of Nibiru are not destined for trivial or domestic application.
The Key will be unlikely to return Simon to you without significant persuasion. And although his sickness will remain stable in the gardens, no un-ascended entity can remain in that place for long.
We hope you will rein in your personal impulses during the next stage of our journey.
The Communion

Brother Ackeron.
Before you proceed with the second rite we urge you to meet us in the sanctum beneath your house.
There is a door in the depths of your undercroft, unknown to you. It leads to a network of spaces that we once used as a scene for our work.
These catacombs were not, we must stress, built by us. They are much older and have seen many things. Before the great witch hunt they served as our primary headquarters in the city. Since that repression they have been sealed and abandoned.
Now that the eye of Nibiru is awakening above Highrook it is time for us to return to them once again.
The Communion

This box contains a collection of wax recordings from the previous owner of the estate, Ms Irma Voltok.
As a prolific writer and performer Ms Voltok began to record her poems and associated thoughts by phonograph. Although this would not usually merit attention from the Communion, the later work of Ms Voltok displays a significant insight, and contains direct references to Nibiruan lore.
As such, I felt compelled to gather what recordings remain and store them for our examination.
Chief Provisioner H.

Brother Ackeron.
Understand that you cannot achieve your ends without our direct assistance. Indeed, if you proceed without our permission then we will be forced to move to more punitive positions.
Do not take this communication lightly, Ackeron. If you defy us then we shall send the hunters to you, and will move to have you permanently defrocked from our order, with all that entails.
We await your apology, and an explanation of why you have proceeded in this insolent manner.
The Communion

The matter of Sophia’s legacy presses on me. This place is dominated by Gideon’s machinations, but in truth I know that Lady Ackeron was a great engineer and far more worthy of recognition. While Gideon meddled, she was an inventor for the ages.
If I do not use my position at Venatus and my own insight, to prove her legacy while I am here… Well, I will betray both of us.
Sophia left many blueprints and sketches behind. I shall work on them. The machine room will have to do.
This is the start of an optional quest for Astor. You do not need to complete this quest to finish the game.

Sophia’s designs appear to draw on so many different lines of inquiry and inspirations I am not even sure where to start! If Gideon was inspired by the arcane potential of this place then perhaps a similar energy enabled Sophia.
She is a woman of science, of course, but there is an almost dreamlike edge to her designs.
If only I could understand Locman Field Complexity as she does!

There are designs among Sophia’s work that I cannot fathom the meaning of. She is either more eccentric than I ever learned, or a genius of the order of Parcius Andronica, or Tergoba The Great.
One of these designs is for some sort of teleportation device! Which means, to my reasoning, that she believes (or even knows) that such modes of transportations must be possible!
Then again, after all she must have seen living here, who knows what one might end up believing… or knowing

I continue to survey Sophia’s writings, drawings, and blueprints. There are designs for listening helmets, grip-enhancing gauntlets, and devices which cause Patalan-type threshold delimiting! I suspect that Ventaus would consider much of her work to be unfounded and indulgent.
Nevertheless I have continued to try to build Sophia’s designs. They do not all work, but they are all remarkable.

An amazing device, designed with such lateral ingenuity. Ether waves have long been theoretical curiosities, but this proves their existence. It is surely a breakthrough for our entire field!
The results of such a discovery should offer Sophia the respect she deserves. Her mind is of a calibre that will echo down the ages with the clarity and brilliance of thought. To play even a small role in that story… I am completed.
On finishing the game this optional story will be concluded.

Someone who haunted this house was a magpie. Always bits and pieces hidden away here and there. Keep finding weird stuff. Makes my tasks harder.
Got Joskel’s gear from the undercoves, though. He told me I might as well look for the Berdholt Knives while I am here. He said Ackeron had them.
Well, Atticus Hawk is going to have them now. -A
This is the start of an optional quest for Atticus. You do not need to complete this quest to finish the game.

It pays to turn over every stone in this rotten estate. An old cairn on the hillside held one of them knives. Thick with mud it were.
I don't think anyone else could even tell what it was. They certainly didn't care when I said I'd chuck it away. Even then I could see it was something special.
They don’t make them like this no more. I cleaned it up of course, all shining and sharp now. I'm good with knives. Like my Pa. -A

Definitely picked up one more of the Berdholt knives. No mistake. Hidden away in a draw for a letter opener. Broken though, but all the bits are there. It is funny what these rich men will pick up and then throw away. People, things.
When you have worked every day in your life you are a bit closer to the things around you. Know how to fix them, and how much they cost.
And this knife cost more than most lives. -A

Now the blades I have found in Ackeron’s collection are becoming as funny as the rest of this ruin.
Was this really made by Berdholt? Whatever... I can say it was, and people will believe it was, and when I sell them all to Finneas in Direwych I will retire and live the good life. People pay well for 'magic' trinkets.
And this is definitely one of them. -A

This blade was deep in the well, as if it had been thrown in there deliberately. Was caked in rust but I cleaned it up and now it shines like a winter moon.
I don’t like to touch it. Cold, but not in temperature. In something else. I don’t know what. Hold it with a rag, or else don’t touch it at all. Struck from some evil metal, and cursed so deeply.
Berdholt was another meddler like Ackeron. I see it now. But it’ll pay for Old Hawk’s house by the sea. -A

This pendant has brought to light another mystery. One which concerns me alone.
Years ago I committed a great failure. I was assigned to combat the devastating Ash Plague. The first victim was a Highrook orderly, interred here, before the autopsy could be conducted. I was intoxicated and absent... I failed to intervene and lost access to the corpse.
Had I been able to examine that body, I might have found the answers I sought.
It is too late to save those who perished then, but this pendant suggests the remains of the orderly might still be here. Perhaps I can find my answers now. I should begin in the archives.
This is the start of an optional quest for Caligar. You do not need to complete this quest to finish the game.

I have found the head of the orderly, like some macabre game of hide and seek. Why did the previous lord choose to treat the body so strangely? I am sure that there is no medical justification for the dismemberment. The post mortem note from the archives leaves me with more questions than answers.
As the dark nature of this estate becomes increasingly clear, I fear that the fate of this body was more to do with ritual than science.

At first I feared that the plague body had been destroyed, but the parts remain. Each buried separately, to avoid the disease returning?
Is this just idiot superstition or is it some other occult practice? Whatever the motives, someone did grim, unfathomable work in this place.
Regardless, I should be able to locate the parts and prepare them for my return to Caincross.

Sometimes I wonder at myself. Would I want to be dragged from a grave to take part in some demonstration or display of knowledge?
I have of course benefitted from such disinterments, yet I begin to feel shame at pulling the fallen back into the light. I myself seek oblivion often enough to sympathise with the sanctity of burial.

I have the bulk of the cadaver, but not yet all the answers. When we leave this place I shall take it with me and back to the laboratory.
Then, perhaps, belatedly, I can right the wrong of the past and create a defence against the Ash Plague. Should it ever come again to Blacksands and the surrounding lands, we might be protected.
Our time at Highrook has been horrifying, but perhaps yet some good can come of it. I shall leave here with a far finer calibre of knowledge than with which I entered.
On finishing the game this optional story will be concluded.

Dear A.
Hows that old ruin treating you? Been chased by any posh ghosts yet?
Anyway, If you are still looking to pick up some extra souvenirs during your job I've got some information for you.
One of the boys told me that he was dropping off a parcel to Lord Ackeron in his study a few months back and the old man opened it with some very fancy knife. Well apparently the Lord managed to trap the knife in his drawer and broke the damn thing. My lad said he was mighty angry about the accident and shouted him out of the house.
Check it out... might be one of the items we are interested in.
J.

Dear A.
You did it ! My buyer is over the moon. He never expected to see a full quartet of those knives on this side of the ocean. But here you are like some foxhound sniffing them all out!
Come round to the den as soon as you get back in town. The contact wants to pay you direct (I've already got my fee) and I reckon you can safely book yourself a carriage there and back. You are going to be rolling in coin for a while my friend, maybe you can buy me a drink to celebrate.
J.
On finishing the game this optional story will be concluded.

Dear A.
Thanks for getting the box back to me. You always were a bit of a bloodhound!
My grapevine also tells me that Highrook is in a right state. Might be a good opportunity to liberate a few things eh? I mention this because a contact of mine has always yearned after a full set of Berdholt knives, and that Highrook by all accounts held one. He'd be willing to pay a princely sum to acquire it.
He reckons that the Lord held a Quillon, Rondel, Poignard and a Jambiya - the full Berdholt quartet. Apparently the lord didn't recognise their value and basically threw them away when he bought the place. You'd need to find them of course, and fix them up if they aren't up to scratch. But a small fortune would be waiting for you if you manage to get them all.
Come on A. you'd be daft not to do it. Start in the cellars, one of my crew swears they saw 'some fancy foreign dagger' there when delivering for the Ackerons last spring.
J.

This book has struck a chord in my heart, re-kindled a desire that I have tried to bury for too long. My dear Ella, my love and muse - lost many years ago...
After she had gone... in another place like this, I saw her in a dream. A dream so real that I would have traded its reality for my own. This book suggests that such meetings might be repeatable!
It seems that in places like Highrook, the veil between dreams and reality become unnaturally thin. Perhaps here, I can glimpse her again? Speak to her? Hold her? I must try!
The book describes a specific seed to be swallowed before sleep, accompanied by a meditative mantra. I could write to my contacts in Verden Row, see if I can acquire one of these kernels.

My experiments in dreaming have begun. The others might grow suspicious of how easily I welcome sleep in this terrible place, but I may never again have the chance to access the many worlds beyond this waking one.
I have not found what I am looking for yet, but I have begun to see… places.
The dream seeds clearly work! I must try to find more of them. Perhaps Lord Gideon or the other occupants of this place had clinical reasons to gather them.

Truly the boundary between this world and others is very frail. Nibiru is most prominent in this manner. But in my dreams the other realms are detectable, too; the land of the dead, the red city, and other realms I have heard of, but never imagined I might glimpse in all their alien glory.
Perhaps I can still find Ella in one of these oneiric domains. Sometimes I feel a hint of her presence, or of others... watching me as I walk in these dreams. A constant feeling of being followed.

In my dream I stood within a small boat, approaching an isle. Tall and impenetrable conifers, as black as night, looming against cliffs of pale stone. The cliffs were like broken bones jutting out of the motionless lake. A dark tower marks the horizon, I saw someone within its crooked arches, Ella? All was silent, even the oars made no sound.
I believe this place to be the isle of the dead, the very gateway to the realm I seek.
Perhaps next time I might find a way to knock, to pass through, to see her once more...

I know now that the land of the dead can be reached. And so my lost fiance, my dear Ella, can also be found. For her to be sent there was the most painful event of my life.
But in this place and in these dreams I finally spoke to my love again. This discovery, this knowledge that I shall be able to reach her, even in life… I can barely stand to put it into words. The feelings defy recording.
I will keep searching in sleep and find that glade again, for I must etch the path there into my mind. For someday, I too will pass into that land beyond life and we might join hands once more.
On finishing the game this optional story will be concluded.

Dear X
Please find your order enclosed.
Firstly, the soporific draught you requested from Caincross. Be aware that its effects can be quite potent. Take a dose in place of your usual nightcap to encourage exotic dreams.
Secondly, the velum from Deep Spire Library. Our operator could not retrieve the entire folio but did extract the page you described.
As usual, there is no return process should you decide that the item is not what you require. We must also remind you that it would be imprudent to mention this, or any of our other transactions, in public.
S.M.

Yesterday Pa made me get some weird neklayce necklace from the cave under the house. Down there the tunnels get all twisted. It was scary. I think maybe smugglurs left it for him!
Pa said not to put it on. But it was shining when I dug it up, like a red star. I wanted to ware wear it really bad. But it hurt when I did, like nettles all over. I took it off quick.
It's in the chapel now and Pa goes there at night and makes strange sounds. Like he's crying? I worry he is putting it on and it is hurting him like it hurt me. I hate it. I want to throw it away but Pa says no.
He is grumpy! He shouted at me the other day, for doing drawing in his study. So now I play outside now. I don't mind, I like warcthing watching the birds, but it feels extra cold today.

I am getting sick. Must have got a cold from the caves and the hurt from the necklace is still there.
I am writing this sitting in the medesin medicine room. I am waiting for Amy to make me a special sleepy drink.
I really do not like being sick. Maybe the necklace has put a curse on me. I'd throw it off the cliff if I could.
Pa do not seem to care, he is still singing his sad songs and doing his big chalk drawings. I can hear him in the chapel from my room sometimes. I hope he doesn't get sick too.
Anyway Amy says its best not to talk to him about it at the moment. She says hes been all quiet and strange of late. He's 'not like his normal self'.

I did it! I took the necklace and hid it in my den. Pa forgot to lock the chapel, so I got in and stole it!
It took a terrble terrible long time to get it here, as it was weird heavy to carry. I am all tired and hurting from being so poorly.
I know I should not have taken it. Pa will be angry. But I done not want it to hurt him or ma! And maybe now its outside the house I might get better too. I hope so
. I'm sorry.

I cannot leave my room. I feel really poorly. I can hear Tubbs outside, scratching. Handsome boy. It is lownlee lonely being all here on my own. I don not like not being able to go awtsi outside.
Amy brings me medysin medicine and biscuits when she can. She even gave me a funny seed I can chew if I'm feeling too upset.
Her pa gave me this carved moonface he made. He says it's to help me sleep.
I like Alfred, he do not talk much but hes always kind to me and lets me do pretend fishing in the well.
I hope I get well soon. Pa says hes working on some special medicine.

I can't do it anymore.. The Communion is more concerned with power over people than mastery of other worlds. They recruited me because of this Lyre, this cursed instrument that I stole on that wet night near Hindberg.
To me it was just fenceable loot, a way to buy food for a week or so. But when I took it to Joskel someone in that shop was watching, paid eyes for the Seekers.
They contacted me the next day, wooed me with lodgings and food. It was the Lyre they wanted, not me. After a week or so they showed their hand... I was now beholden to them, a thief who they could hand in whenever I stepped out of line.
For years I assisted them. But no more, I will leave, go into hiding. They will not have me or this damn Lyre!
V

Pilgrims, your progress is both impressive and concerning. I fear that you will soon need more than your natural wits to proceed.
Before my exile, the Seekers charged me with locating an ancient and powerful 'Thought Condenser' within Highrook. It lay in pieces across the estate, split and hidden by a previous owner.
In order to find it, I was given a divining ring, attuned to the condenser's energies. I did not complete the task, and when I fled I took the ring with me.
I pass it to you now. In the hope that you might complete the hunt. My memory is unclear, but you might do well to begin your search in the dining room or the laboratory. I hope you can succeed where I failed.
V

The fourth circle is breached! Highrook has become wreathed in some foul mist. I tried to join you, but each time I entered I found myself turned around. I only hope that this message finds its way through.
The Communion is en-route, they are trying to remove any trace of their involvement or reference to their members... They have summoned 'Devourers' to the estate. Immaterial wraiths that will destroy any occult energies they can find.
But perhaps I can still help. There is a crate deep in the cellars, the location is attached. It contains an item that brought me to the communion's attention. I have never forgiven myself for the way I acquired it and the path it put me on. But if it can help you now, it might form part of my own reparations with the past.
V.

Fellow Mecanist Astor.
Firstly, we commend you on your commitment to this investigation. A paper on your findings will be most welcome in the Institute Archives.
Judging from your description of the modified locks, it appears that Lord Ackeron has been receiving assistance from the Seekers. The Communion has developed an alternative configuration to our standard locking mechanism and uses it to secure their hideouts and archives.
Their work is far from sophisticated though, and we have included a Mk1 Skeleton Key with this letter to enable you to bypass their crude revisions. We wish you good fortune in your work. May the cogs turn your way!
Venatus Institute Assembly

Atticus is a simple thug. The man clearly has no understanding or appreciation of anything that he can't immediately hold or see.
He is an unsophisticated bear, something that I might even find appealing in other circumstances! But I must remain focussed on our task, and advocate for brains over brawn.
I am sure that Bleakhurst sent me here because of my interest in arcane texts. They may disapprove of my specialism publicly, but they benefit from it privately.
Despite common belief, many of the occult theories promoted by the Seekers have authentic grounds. It would be a great vindication if I were to unearth proof here that my focus of study was not in vain.

It is difficult not to despise that lump, Atticus. If we did not require the presence of someone to hunt and carry then I would have sent him away, or at least petitioned to the others that we did so.
The horrors of Highrook are not those which we can beat with hands like clubs! They are not something we can take out into the garden, hit with a spade, and then bury in the thin dirt, as Atticus no doubt wishes to do. This place is a puzzle box of many-dimensional complexity!
As an example, whatever ritual incantations Lord Ackeron may have uncovered. It is only my learning and insight that will allow us to engage with them in the correct manner.

Ever since we began to assemble the second ritual, my dreams have begun to linger into the waking hours. They add some tincture of themselves to all of reality after the fact. As if they are attempting to reach out to me beyond the confines of sleep.
What if all dreams are not simply the struggles of the unconscious mind, but a sort of reception of a transmission? We have seen from the mecanists that such remote transmissions are possible via mechanical means, so why not something of the flesh across time and space?
The more I dream here, the more I am convinced that such nighttime visions might offer a very real conduit to other worlds and histories.

Another rite assembled and hopefully another step towards the culmination of our task. Even with the knowledge I am gathering I am keen to be finished with this assignment.
It is a sort of hell to be trapped here with these people. I have remained polite and professional - of course I have! - but never in my life have I had to share a space with a brute beast like Atticus. My admiration for his physique has all but faded. He sees nothing and he knows nothing. Did they sew together the butcher's leftovers and bake a loaf for the brain?
For a while I thought I might speak to the others about my 'somnambulant theories' but it feels as if my words slide off them too, like rain on oilskin. Without my dear Ella I am destined to be forever alone in my thoughts and ambitions.

I am no longer using the phonograph to journal my reflections of the 'moon fly' experiments. Instead, I am recording the journeys directly. I am attempting to describe the visions as they occur.
The phonograph has been most useful in this research, but some recordings have turned out more disturbing than I expected.
One session in particular saw my narration transform into a stream of pained whispers, in a language I do not know.
Listening back to the recording left me so disturbed I had to retire with a measure of laudanum.
I doubt that there is anything of sense in this recording, but the cylinder is attached if by chance I wish to re-examine my unsettling glossolalia.

My 'voyages' are becoming more intense, and the recordings more garbled. I now believe I am always drawn to the same place, an unnatural, shadowed isle lit by the flickering rays of a burning moon.
The recordings are often confused and hard to transcribe (such as the one I include here), and sometimes even seem to have captured other voices than my own.
I have written several drafts for new poems immediately after these visions. But the results are always unreadable, the pages criss-crossed with garbled phrases and arcane symbols.
I am hoping that my attempts will gain clarity over time. Perhaps it is simply a matter of adjusting the dose?

I had my final voyage last night, the culmination of my terrible visions!
I was transported to an unearthly black desert. A terrible wasteland lit by the fevered rays of that burning moon.
The land itself was strewn with grim lakes and wreathed in bright mists. Everything was vivid and cold. I could smell the pools and hear the discharge of static in the air.
The moon filled the sky above and I felt suffocated, crushed, as if underwater. Figures all composed of ethereal light flickered in and out of that realm, stumbling like automatons, lost pilgrims staggering across the barren land.
It was too much, too much. I am quaking now with the memory. I am sealing my last ampoule here, along with the device I used to filter the extract. I will not go back. I cannot go back.

I am unwell. My experiments have left me scarred and it does not heal. I have not used the extract for days. Yet, when I close my eyes, that blasphemous landscape appears once more.
Even in my waking hours the shadows around Highrook transform into the spires of that forsaken land and I feel the cold heat of that sickening moon on my back.
My adventures took a step too far and I came here to destroy the drafts I have written, to burn them in the forge. Yet I could not. Something (pride perhaps) would not let me do this.
I will take them to the archives, where they might be safely hidden. Perhaps their terrible inspiration will one day be worth this nightmarish tariff.

Dream Draught! A tonic frowned upon by the dispensaries of Caincross Yard. It is said to be a powerful soporific, and one that elicits wild dreams.
Caligar studies the bottle, swirling the contents around.
Lord Ackeron was growing the leaves that make this potion... If we were to use a dose in place of the Night Lamp when we sleep, we might find out why.

A package of some sort has been delivered.
Atticus shifts the leather bound box with his boot.
I didn't see anyone drop it off, but I guess we need to keep an eye out for any other stuff that might appear.

Indeed Atticus. I recall that the Ackerons often employed couriers to gather items from the town.
Especially so as they began to withdraw from BlackSands themselves.

Nothing from Direwych ever works properly! It's a nest of grifters down there.
But I am glad the Lady was startin' to notice her husband's decline. Let us hope she got out before he got 'er involved in his wicked plans.

It is a relief to find more evidence of Lady Ackeron. Sophia was a keen amateur scientist... I made her acquaintance at various lectures in town - a truly remarkable woman. I pray we might still find her safe.
The device is a mecanist design, but it is unfamiliar to me. It seems to be some sort of mental imager. Even if it did not suit her needs it might be useful for ours.

The equipment in this schoolroom here might also be of use. The chair is designed to support machine-enhanced learning.
Vitali strokes his beard, pondering the possibilities.
If we can find the time within our investigations, we would do well to make use of the training offered here.

The world melts into a watery gloom. A vision shimmers into view, as if stepping through a waterfall.
Hello?... are you from the outside? Have you come to take me home? Please take me home... It is so strange here, roots like worms, and worms like roots. I don't like it, and I can't get out.
I am slow and empty... Am I falling asleep... Am I dreaming?

The one who brought me here, won't take me home. She comes and goes, singing like a howling star, her head all broken up..
Simons image begins to waver.
Please... tell Pa I'm sorry about the necklace... and... I miss him... and Ma and Amy and... Tubbs.

I am the Key, the opener of gates, instrument of the End. I am the keeper of Nibiru's secret paths.
You have come knocking for me to return the boy? I will not. He is dreaming in the garden of the First Circle. He will sleep with the shadows on the shore, a tribute to the End.
Turn back, fleshlings, these roads are not for you.

What in the hell was that? It felt like the sky had become an ocean and drowned us all! the Ackeron boy... like a ghost, half here and half elsewhere, thin and hollow!
Atticus rubs his eyes with grubby fingers.
And that beast, that horror! Its head like a broken root... Was it real? And if so, what has Gideon done?

That entity... was an instrument of Nibiru, a lesser demon of the End. Something I thought that I would never witness.
Vitali shivers, but his response betrays an edge of excitement.
