The Key is the custodian of the First Circle. The sentinel on the shore. I have read of such beings, but never dreamed I would see one!

Perhaps the window through which The Key spoke has not fully closed. There is a mark here on the ground, an uncanny rift or fissure. And a card here seemingly dropped by the boy.
Caligar plucks the Key Card from the grimy boards
We should monitor this scar, in case its presence conjures more nightmares.

Very wise, Caligar.
We need more information on how these unholy rituals operate - and who is involved. I suspect that there are more occult texts locked in the secure cases of the archives.
I will send word to my colleagues at Venatus. Perhaps they can provide us with assistance in accessing them.

This does not bode well. The first evidence of Lord Ackeron we find, and it's a garbled, paranoid rant...
Perhaps Gideon was trying to escape the Communion's grasp, or perhaps his occult obsessions really had driven him insane.
Astor looks disturbed.

I ain't no detective, but perhaps the Lord was up to no good and this is him trying to cover his tracks.
Atticus brows knit together with suspicion.
He could be trying to set up someone to take the blame for whatever happened to his family.
Or maybe he just went mad, sitting up 'ere with all his weird books!

Do not be so quick to judge! Lord Ackeron was an accomplished academic, I don't think we can simply dismiss his writings as the babblings of a madman.
I feel there is truth in his words - disturbing though they be - but it is too soon to say what this outburst really means.

The fragments have formed the 'Opening Eye', the ritual that the Seekers urged Gideon to complete! It is a window into Nibiru's hidden domain.
Vitali shuffles around the chamber, nervous, but excited.
It might seem foolish, but I think we must perform this rite to further our investigations.

Vitali... Are you mad?
These evil rites should be burned, not performed. We should look for the Ackerons here, in the real world!
Atticus shakes his head vigorously.
Gideon may have been insane, but we need not follow him into his lunacy.

I hear you Atticus, but it's clear that Gideon was determined to carry out this ritual. Perhaps we can find fresh tracks by replicating his actions.
If you trusted my judgement during the Keel Fever epidemic, then please, remain in step with us now.

Aye Ms. Caligar, you pulled me and my boys through that outbreak. I still owe you for that.
Atticus wrings his hands, uncertain...
I am not happy with Vitali's plan, it won't end well.... but I'll do as you ask... for now.

I see you also appreciate a good drink Atticus. It has been some time since I've been able to share a tipple with someone who doesn't want my opinion on some illness or another.
A boil here, a rash there... but not you ... you seem in good health. Strong and stalwart, capable of enduring when others might fold and break.

Was born this way, you know?
Helps to be built like this when you are luggin' stuff around the piers all day.
An' a drink after a days work is only natural. I like to work hard and play hard, if you know what I mean.

Is that it? Have the horrors stopped?
Atticus holds up his hands in a questioning gesture.
If that's all these demons have to offer, then their bark is worse than their bite.

Yes, we have sealed the fissure that was formed during the Ritual.
Vitali handles the seal with reverence.
And it appears that even Nibiru must acknowledge our progress.

Now the incursions have ceased perhaps we can return to locating the Lady Sophia?
It seems she was designing some sort of communication device. With luck, Sophia might have her prototype with her. If we construct our own version, we might be able to make contact.

I see Mayor Aliston is as conceited as always. His presumption that all city events require his involvement is so tiresome.
I suspect that Bleakhurst has been involved more for political point-scoring than out of respect for our knowledge. But perhaps I can track down the books that Ackeron 'borrowed' from us last year...
Vitali sighs and rolls his eyes.

Indeed Vitali, I am equally tired of Aliston's petty machinations. But the High Council provides us with the bulk of our funding, and as such we are obliged to respond.
At least they have provided us with some of tools to begin our work. We should take this supply crate to the Machine Room, where I can extract its contents.

I don't much like Aliston either, but he pays well.
An' I certainly don't trust bookworms like this Ackeron chap. Nothin' but trouble in all those old tomes...
Atticus shuffles impatiently.
Let's find these upmarket fools and get out of here.

Spoken like a true Aldwerther!
Vitali shakes his head dismissively.
Don’t worry my friend, you will be away from the bookworms and back with the woodworms soon.

Fewer insults, more action. Our remaining colleague, a doctor from Caincross, will be joining us tomorrow. We should prepare for her arrival.
Astor draws a mecanist keydriver from her belt and approaches the crate.

As I suspected, the aftermath of our ritual has invited new terrors to the house. Perhaps they are linked to that cursed mark in the Chapel.
Caligar seems more intrigued than concerned.
We should use our skills to remove or destroy them before they damage us or the property.

At least we can rid ourselves of these invading fiends. They are not all untouchable phantoms.
Atticus cracks his knuckles.

It appears so Atticus.
Though take care when facing them, they still exhibit unnatural powers.
Caligar clasps her gloved hands together.
We must examine each new entity carefully, in order to counter their intrusions!

A familiar tale I'm afraid, the aspirations of the wife being subject to the ambitions of the husband.
Astor shakes her head in frustration.
Sophia was a skilled inventor in her own right. Perhaps if her research had been pursued, instead of her husbands', this whole debacle might have been avoided.

Regardless of their marital squabbles, we should investigate the device Sophia was designing. If it can visualise hidden signals then it might be of great use to us.
And by pursuing her design, we will likely find more traces of the Lady herself.

I truly hope so Vitali.
I am convinced that she would not have been a willing participant in her husband's occult practices.

The detector begins to hum, and a projection flickers into life. A ghostly image of the Lady Sophia appears before you.
Wait? What? Who are you? You managed to duplicate my device? This is a miracle!
Can you hear me? See me?

You must be close, the field does not reach far. Where are you? In the house?
She seems anxious and drained, kneeling at the edge of a dark subterranean cliff. A makeshift camp is visible behind her.
We must hurry, the connection will not last long.

It's me Sophia, Jane Astor. I'm sorry we had to meet again under these awful circumstances.
The image begins to shimmer, as the power runs low.
I am here to find you - with a team sent by the council. Where are you? Are you safe?

Ah Jane, it is good to hear your voice... It has been too long. But where I am, I cannot truly say.
I followed Gideon through a secret door in the cellars, a hidden entrance that led to an even deeper labyrinth. And now I am trapped in a maze of strange tunnels and eerie chambers. I have water and food, but...
The projections sputters like a guttering candle.

I am mapping out the surrounds. Perhaps the Seekers have a secret hideout or shrine down here. If I can find it then I might find a path to my son.
I left the last of my notes in the forge, the code is ....
You manage to note down the sequence as the image dissolves.

Another delivery? In the middle of all this chaos?
Seems like the rumours haven't put off the errand-boys yet!

Apologies for my late arrival. I had to visit a patient in Direwych yesterday. The fellow had developed 'Calxins Compliance', bones like rubber, most intriguing!
Dr Caligar's fingers lace and unlace.
Coincidentally, my guild was summoned here recently to tend to the Ackerons' son. He was suffering from an unusual infection. Unfortunately my colleagues were unable to diagnose the cause.

Dr Caligar, your late arrival is of no matter, we have barely unpacked our own equipment!
The mansion is somewhat disturbed and various chambers are inaccessible, sealed with mecanist locks.
I believe that one of these locations might house a simple laboratory that you could make use of - when we gain access...

Ah, I suspected as much, my colleagues sensed foul play when they visited here before. Lord Ackeron was adamant that our team should not investigate without his supervision.
Luckily, a junior analyst had the foresight to retain the laboratory code. We should be able to gain access using the copy I have here.

Very smart, Ms Caligar! But it don't surprise me.
You were as sharp as a blade when you fixed up me an' my crew from keel fever last spring... saved us from a right wreckin' you might say.
Atticus seems almost coy.
I owe you one... If you need any alchemy supplies or help with shiftin' stuff just let me know.

Science! Unlike the chaotic missteps of lore-seekers and ritual, a mechanical solution has yielded actual progress.
Astor hooks her thumbs into her tool belt and looks on defiantly.
Sophia is alive! And we can contact her through the very machine she devised. We must re-activate the field phone and find a way to rescue her.

Aye Ms Astor! A relief... But it seems that Lady Sophia is now trapped in the tunnels beneath the mansion. With luck, her only peril will come from whatever Seekers might be down there.
And, however smart they might be, scholars ain't no fighters, and I reckon Lady Sophia can handle herself if need be.

You underestimate the abilities of a scholar, Atticus. Perhaps I should demonstrate to you what we are capable of.
Vitali grins menacingly.
But enough! The Lady gave us access to the Forge, let us see what can be found there.

Interesting... A Groundskeeper and his daughter attended to the family, taking their own lodgings in the old well house. It appears that the father was also suspicious of Gideon's behaviour and had been stashing some of the Lord's tools and relics.
I am not sure if this will help or hinder us...

Alfred Blayne I think his name is... I'd see 'im now and again at the docks in Aldwerth or at Direwych Market.
He seemed like a decent fella, bit of a dreamer, and a bit too fond of smoking, but a good sort. Heard he'd adopted some of the orphans with his missus.
I hope him and his daughter are safe somewhere...

We should pay attention to their journals if we can find more. It's remarkable how overlooked the domestics can be.
No doubt the Ackerons' servants had accepted all manner of occult deliveries, and had access to the private chambers of the family.

Yet more proof that these tablets are essential to composing a second rite.
Vitali rubs his hands, with cold, or with excitement?
We should complete the assembly and attempt the ritual... There is further enlightenment to be found!

I cannot share in your enthusiasm, Vitali... Nothing but chaos and disorder results from these occult affairs.
And more to the point, how will this help Sophia? She is not in Nibiru, as far as we can tell. She is still trapped in the Seekers' old sanctum.

The rites we are assembling dissolve the border between our world and the Unseen Twin. For a brief time, places of power - the chapel, the sanctum, the gates of Nibiru - become connected.
Vitali raises his book as if to accentuate the point
These windows of opportunity might allow Sophia to find her way back to us.

The fragments are made whole, the second circle awaits. We can now call upon the Song, the Cup and the Dreamers of the Ruins.
Vitali strides around the chamber brandishing his notes.
It may seem hazardous. But I am confident that we will fare better than Lord Gideon - by mastering these rituals I am sure we can resolve our quest.

Your confidence seems almost zealous, Vitali!
I hope you are not becoming seduced by this noxious myth in the same way that Gideon did?

Nonsense! I am merely more informed than Gideon was. He had but scattered private research, I am backed by the library of Bleakhurst.
Vitali frowns in Astor's general direction
Besides, what alternatives do we have? This ritual might be the only way to provide the Lady Sophia with an opportunity to escape.

I fear that Lady Ackeron is close to delirium.
It is hard to say how she will behave... judging by her last transmission she is as likely to press forward as she is to return to the surface.

This is emberite! A miraculous find. It can dissolve grime from cogwork, bolster the strength of metals, and improves conductivity in electromagnetic devices.
In Venatus our reserves of this are kept under lock and key. If we have any tools we can upgrade, we should take them to the forge and use emberite to improve them.

What has Ackeron done? Has he really offered up his own child to some eldritch horror? Real monsters or rotten Seekers, it don't matter to me. It's abduction, plain an' simple.
Atticus clenches his fists.
We must find the boy, but I don't care if Gideon is ever seen again.

Yes Atticus, he seems to have made a pact with the Communion, or the entities they revere. And to hide this from his wife. Such arrogance. Sophia Ackeron is no idiot, her intellect is easily a match for her husband - she will not be fooled.
Astor adjusts her goggles anxiously
But of more pressing concern... who is this Key? A Demon, a Seeker or something else?

If my memory serves me correctly, the Key is an instrument of Nibiru, the chief doorkeep of the Unseen Twin.
If Gideon has awoken such an entity, then we will face more fearsome dangers than the Communion's thugs.

Enough! My children are not to be crushed so casually, they are but grubs who stumbled into your world.
The window is closed. A seal is returned, though it will not help you.
Flail against the circles, you will break yourselves on our walls. Return to the quiet vale of ignorance while you still can.

So Sophia discovered what we already know. I cannot imagine her distress...
I know she had already lost faith in Gideon's intentions, but this discovery must have left her feeling entirely alone.
A tragic revelation indeed, I hope that her reaction didn't lead her into rash or dangerous actions. She clearly intended to take matters into her own hands.

Our revelry is disturbed once again. There is a knocking at the door. Do you wish to join the Feast of the Old Blood?
Dark liquid spills from the brim of the demon's goblet.
Seekers and fools are both welcome! We have such dark dreams to share.

Instruments of the End. Envoys of Nibiru. I call on you to release our companions to this world.
Vitali trembles... his eyes wide in awe
By the power of the golden wheel and the six blades I command you to relinquish your hold on this family!

Do not threaten us, fleshling.
The child still flickers here like a candle, his roots meld with our soil.. we will not release him...
But you may have a pilgrim in his place, a returning herald, ready to sing to you of the glory he has seen.

Thank heavens... you managed to reactivate the field phone. But I fear the connection will not hold for long...
I am still in the labyrinthine tunnels, somewhere beneath the house. I cannot find my way back to the cellars... the door I followed Gideon through has vanished.
Sophia shakes her head in frustration.

This place is unsettling. The architecture is a strange jumble of hewn rock and ancient stonework.
Tunnels burrow straight ahead, yet loop back upon themselves. Twisting shafts puncture through the corridors bringing illumination from somewhere above and dragging fetid air from below. I do not wish to be here any longer than necessary.

Please Sophia, stay strong! We will assist you however we can...
Astor adjusts the device, attempting to get a better signal.
Have you seen anything there that could help direct us?

Very little I am afraid, the chambers are filled with debris - broken crates and shards of etched pale stone, like the tablets Simon found buried on the clifftops last spring.
Although, perhaps that itself is worth investigating? Take my compass - it's in a box in the guest rooms. Maybe you can locate some of these tablets yourself?

We will do so Lady Ackeron. I shall follow the trail above as you do below. Perhaps we can gain knowledge from these tablets and turn it to our advantage.
The signal begins to fade.
Stay safe, we will be in contact again soon...

I found some of my husband's work. Within one of the darker alcoves was an improvised study, of sorts. A small desk built from stacked crates, overflowing with damp paperwork.
The signal flickers briefly as Sophia attends to the machine.
An etched stone tablet was resting beside some sort of transcription.

It is unclear when Gideon was last here, but his notes refer to a ritual of some sort, the 'Second Circle'?
Sophia holds up a crumpled page, her hand trembling
This mentions a document box hidden in the archives on a specific shelf. The box appears to hold something important to his research.

We will search for this container Mrs Ackeron. But I am concerned for your health, and for that of your son.
The Doctor leans closer to the projected image
Do the notes mention Simon or his condition at all?

Gideon either thinks Simon is safe, or is too transfixed with his own dark obsessions to care anymore!
Sophia is visibly shaken, but pulls herself together
I will leave the papers here as I found them, and continue my explorations. I must stay focused, a strange numbing reverie pulls at me!

I found it! The Seekers' Den.. and... perhaps another entrance to Nibiru... Could this be where Simon is being held?
Sophia is clearly exhausted, but is energised by the discovery.
It was during one of my increasingly dazed wanderings that I... a makeshift chapel of sorts. It is larger than the other grottos and decorated with rotting wooden benches, arranged like pews.

Where the pulpit might be is a large stonework door.
It is made of the same pale mineral as the tablets and holds an ancient engraving that depicts a goblet of some kind, held within two broken circles.
To my dismay it has no handles and will not open for me...

The walls are lined with decorative tiles, some of which are open, revealing hidden compartments. The chapel at home is lined with the same tiles. Perhaps you can see what you can find there?
I fear for my safety and my for my mind... I dare not wait in the chamber itself, but I will remain nearby in the hope that I will be alerted to anyone arriving.

Be careful Sophia...
Do not attempt to confront the Seekers directly. We know that they have little regard for anyone beyond their circle.

My fear is transforming into a kind of dream state. I hear voices and footsteps, but they are not real!
The image of Sophia blurs as she shakes her head sorrowfully.
I am sure that something is watching me from down the darkened corridors. I was scared, but I waited...

Eventually the Seekers returned. I hid nearby, listening to them talk of 'The Song' and 'The Blade'.
My husband was not among them, but they are clearly hoping to open the door with a ritual drawn from the tablets.

I think we might be close to that ritual ourselves, Lady Ackeron. And, if so, we may be able to open the door from the Chapel here.
When a ritual is performed a conduit opens between Nibiru and our world.. Doors open - real and symbolic - and things can pass between one point in time and space to another.
It is like a network of cosmic points that can be briefly traversed.

So we can open one of these damn magic doors and get the lady back?
Atticus cracks his knuckles
I hate all this ritual bilge, but if we can bring the lady home and lock the rest in, then what are we waitin' for?

Sophia shakes her head, tears in her eyes
If Simon is still trapped in there, then I don't want to return! There would be nothing to return to.
The Seekers left a tablet in the Chapel, it is nearly complete and obviously important. I do not understand its meaning but I will describe the symbols to you now.
Please, do what you can to stop this nightmare!

Sophia... do not lose hope...
I ... We... will find you.
The field phone buzzes with the soft rain of dying static, and then falls silent

This note confirms what I already suspected. Simons illness was some form of otherworldly malady, contracted when his father involved the boy in his occult research.
Dr Caligar adjusts her mask and begins to pace around the room.
No wonder my colleagues couldn't identify the cause of the problem. I only wish I'd had been there to examine him, his description of the ailment, and the pain, is most intriguing.

The poor mite. His father is nuthin' but a coward... sending his son into the undercoves because he daren't go there himself!
Meddlin' in the dark arts is stupid enough, but including kids in such danger is unforgivable!
And yet he'd look down at us Docksfolk if he passed us in the street... Bah!

Atticus, it is not our role to judge Lord Ackeron's morals, simply to follow his trail.
Vitali opens his arms in an appeal for calm..
But, we can agree that the son's illness was related to his fathers work... We should try to find this necklace. I would like to know how it is involved in the Seekers' plans.

I felt the melody stop... the chords resolve... my minstrel broken by your interference.
What is it you want, half-lives? You and your ilk form such tuneless interruptions. Your world is made of whispers. You are not worthy to enter the refrain.

We are not as weak as you suppose!
We can see the tendrils of your corruption. We have dealt with all your loathsome minions so far...
Astor is trembling, but defiant.
Your unnatural order will only decay under its own corruption! Return those that you have taken and be gone forever!

You wish to see them again, yes? Then take this gift, alongside the seal which I must offer.
The Cup reaches out from the electrifying mist, and drops a small silver bell on the ground in front of you.
Call your companions with this if you want, but they are not the only ones who are listening...

What was that thing? It seemed almost human, yet twisted into a horrible travesty of life. It has been driven off, but not for good. I can still hear its cries from across the estate.
The Mecanist looks relieved, but concern soon returns to her face.
But where is Sophia? She was supposed to have returned via the ritual. Did this creature emerge instead of her?

Yes Ms Astor, I think you are correct.
It might even be that Sophia chose to enter the shadowed isle herself during the rite. If so, she is now in Nibiru, in pursuit of her child. We might only be able to contact her again via further ritual.

I believe that her 'replacement', is some form of reanimated life. I have heard of such 'zombies' but never seen one with my own eyes. How does it still function? What magic lies in its blood?
Caligar shakes herself out of the reverie.
It seems to have some connection to this place though, a manor Key Card fell from its rags as it fled.

GRRRrrgnnnngh.... th.. the... song releassses me.....
A crooked shadow emerges from the mist and lumbers towards the house.
Mmmmmnnnn that smell.. so sweeeeet.. the stolen blood... the stolen sun..

What evil has been visited on us now? A rotting ghoul, spouting gibberish and bile.
Atticus clenches his fists.
Begone you skin-draped horror or I will beat your fetid frame back into the earth!

...Grrnhhannaaaaahh.. to be reborn.. to make anew.....
the scent of memories....
The wretched thing stumbles around, hissing with rage.
... liess.... false songs.... false dreamsssssss...

The ghoul is searching clumsily for something, knocking furniture over and flailing against the walls.
The turning... gnnngg.... the burning...
It mimes indecipherably.
... the edge, the glint... aarrrrhh...

Why will this thing not die? Even if it would be a second death...
Astor shakes her head in confusion.
It seems to be driven by more than just the will of its masters.

The thing staggers about the chamber, howling like an injured bear.
.. mmmmyyy home.... agggghh.. betrayed.. ik ik ikkk
.. sweeeeet moonlit eyes...
Anger burns in its empty sockets.

It's.. wait.. I recognise that voice.
Atticus fists bunch and his eyes narrow.
It's Alfred.. the groundskeeper.. part of him is still in there, trapped, angry, wild with fear....
On hearing its name called the ghoul howls again, and launches itself at Hawk, its broken fingers clawing at the air.

Poor fella! As much as we did him a favour here, I can't help but feel for the old man.
Atticus frowns wearily, anger rising in his eyes.
He didn't go into this like Lord Gideon, hungry for power and careless of others. He was just trying to protect those around him.

Yes, a sad end indeed.
I wonder how long this resurrection would have lasted, even without our interventions.
There appears to have been some internal motor keeping the corpse running. An augmented heart of sorts, wasting sinew intertwined with metallic bands.

However it was engineered, this thing obeys no natural law!
Astor grips the clockwork heart in her fist, its surfaces still slick with dark blood.
I've had enough! We should send this evil machine back to Nibiru. Show them that we cannot be held back from our mission.

At last, the fog begins to clear. The Seekers are trying to contact Nibiru, a mythical domain of cosmic power. An unseen isle that lies hidden outside of natural time and space.
Vitali frowns, looking concerned, yet excited..
Engaging with these histories is enlightening, but it is also dangerous.

I think we can assume that Gideon has already begun his journey down that path. The chapel has clearly been used for ritualistic practices.
Astor examines the thick oak door
We can assume it was locked to prevent his family from discovering his work. If he was hiding his activities here, then what might await us in the other sealed chambers?

The old man paid more attention to the boy than his own father did.
Atticus sighs wearily.
It must have been hard adopting Amy on his own, and keeping up with the labours here. But even then, he still found time for the Ackeron boy.

As is often the case, those with the least to give, offer the most.
My hands might be trained by Caincross, but my boots are still muddy from the alleys of Direwych.
Perhaps there is some inspiration to be found in this trinket. Highrook has sent guidance in dreams before, we should sleep with it as our focus.

Was one of those summoned fiends the siren that seduced poor Alfred? The foul banshee that tricked him to his death.
Atticus snarls, weighing the club in his hand.
Poor old man. He was just trying to protect others! Only to end up danced around like a rotting flesh puppet!

I fear so Atticus. The groundskeeper spoke of the Song in his journal. She seemed to hypnotise him.... a poisoned chalice indeed.
Caligar shakes her head sadly.
As if our earthly temptations are not trouble enough.

Indeed, the demons of the second circle are drunken deities, delirious and deviant!
Vitali folds his book closed and frowns.
They delight in exploring pain and cruelty for their own amusement - which makes me wary of this 'gift' they have given us.

A ragged hole has formed in the air, a spectral window into the unseen twin. A familiar face appears through the mist.
My friends.. it is you! I am sorry I did not return... I took the chalice door when it was offered... to find Simon!
I had to step through, into this forsaken place. But now I am lost and chasing shadows... you must help!

Sophia, we are still here, we are finding our way to you. You will soon be free of this torment, I promise.
Astor reaches out, but her hand drifts through the vision, as if trailing in a river of smoke.
Is there anything we can do to help from here?

I... I don't know... At times I think I see Simon, or even Gideon, but it is only a twisted spire or charred shrub.
Perhaps check my son's room? There is a spare card in the archives if you know where to look.
Half-seen brambles writhe at her feet, both here and there, in this mix of worlds

You must endure, Lady Ackeron! We have almost breached the Third Circle, where the higher authority of Nibiru begins.
Vitali clutches his books with fervour.
If we can prove our mastery of their words, your captors must surely bow to our wishes.

A ragged hole has formed in the air, a spectral window into the unseen twin. A forlorn figure appears through the mist.
Who... who are you? You aren't one of those demons are you?
They took my Pa! They took his heart, put in some ticking clock, made him into a monster! I tried to follow! To protect him like he protected me!

Slow down, child.
We can help you, but first we need to know how you got there.
Vitali paces the room, scratching his head
Where are you now? Can you describe your surroundings?

I'm in some deep hall, made of this stone, an evil stone - my eyes slide off it and I swear it's whispering!
A grand shadowed vault is half-visible behind Amy as she stares trance-like through the summoning rift.
There's writing on the walls too, but I don't understand it. I wish I'd used that book Pa got me now, instead of shoving it under my bed...

All will be well Amy.
Atticus looks perturbed, as if something in Amy's manners or features stirs a memory.
You ain't expected to be able to read this evil tongue... In fact its best that you can't. It's because of these cursed words that we ended up in this mess.

Amy looks around in dismay, as if she can hear but not see.
I just followed him is all. A lady... I thought he was engaged in a tryst! But then they both vanished... and I, I followed and...
The image dissolves into flickering motes.

A ragged hole has formed in the air, a spectral window into the unseen twin. Gideon's gaunt features appear from the shadows.
Who are you? Did the Communion send you? Well, it is no matter, we are all lost now...
The geometry of the ruins here is unfathomable, it traps me like a grand mathematical puzzle.

Lord Ackeron! You must focus! How far have you progressed?
Vitali leans forward as if to shake the vision by its shoulders.
You must tell me what wards and words to use to reach where you are now... and further!

I was close, so close, but the machinations of Nibiru have bested me, even these tools cannot help me now.
He casts down a tattered volume and looks up, tears cutting pale paths across his grimy face.
There is no ascension, there is no reward. I have failed.

Do not dare hide in your misery! This tragedy is of your own making. Your arrogance has dragged your family into the depths with you.
Astor shakes with rage.
Stay there yourself for all I care, but we will return those you have forsaken!

A ragged hole has formed in the air, a spectral window into the unseen twin. A hollow child appears through the mist.
Mama? Is that you? I am so tired... The Clock says I will sleep soon, and the roots will take care of me.
It's very cold, but you get used to it, until you cant really feel anything at all.

Simon! Don't go to sleep.
Caligar peers at the hollow child and then steps closer.
You can feel the warmth here? Now? towards my voice?

It does feel nice... like the kitchen when Amy's cooking.
The ghostly image leans forward blindly as if trying to touch the real world. Something falls from the boys pocket.
Is Amy here? Or is she there? Is she asleep too?
I- I .. want to come home...

It is clear that Alfred was intercepting and hiding a number of Lord Ackeron's deliveries.
Amy spotted his actions easily, so I wonder why Gideon did not notice?

The lords and ladies often miss what happens right under their noses, especially when it comes to us low-folk.
Atticus offers a bittersweet grin.
Fortunately there are some advantages to being 'invisible'.

I expect Lord Ackeron was too absorbed in otherworldly matters to track the mundane actions of his staff.
Vitali hurries the conversation along
Even so, it will undoubtedly aid us to recover whatever tools the groundskeeper had pilfered.

I presume that these twisted words mean you can summon up those fiends again, Vitali?
This time let us not be so timid. We have overcome enough of their evil already! Lets get the Ackerons out of there!
... and Amy too, that poor girl. To lose a father and then to be pulled into the same nightmare...
Atticus shakes his head sorrowfully.

Indeed, there are only a few gates now left between us and the heart of Nibiru! Each step we take bolsters our power, raising us to adepts who cannot be ignored.
This incantation will call upon the third circle, the ring of charred ash, where the makers' hammers ring out in the endless chimes of transformation.

Then let's get on with it!
Astor fidgets nervously, pulling at her gloves fingers and pacing around the group.
As much as I despise this blasphemous practice, it seems we have little choice.

The cycles are disturbed once again... Not by the deluded Lord, but by his hired hunters instead.
Though it matters not, your complaints be drowned by cog and hammer. Nibiru's wheel turns over you now, crushing your bones, and you do not even see it.
Giant organic machines turn in the shadows around the Clock.

Instruments of the End. Envoys of Nibiru. I call on you to release our companions to this world.
Vitali trembles... his eyes wide in awe
We have mastered your rituals and broken your gates! Relinquish your hold on this family!

Do not threaten us. Your power is paper thin! I shine through your flesh, you are naught but shadows to us.
The Lantern gestures, and wraithlike sentries begin to materialise across the estate.
You have broken no gates. Nibiru is already here, it lives alongside you! It lives inside you!

Gah.. what is this now... evil eyes? Were these things always here, as the demon suggested?
Atticus spits in disgust.
Reminds me of Senville Gaol, sentries on every corner... and just as corrupt!

Yes, I think they have always been present, just invisible to our mortal eyes. They are observers for Nibiru, conjured machines that watch and whisper to their makers.
Vitali ponders for a moment
We should destroy them to break the connection to their masters, blind them, as it were...

How can such things even exist? Like the groundskeeper... constructs of flesh, metal and dark energy.
These 'Watchers' can be moved to some degree, but are bound to the rooms that they are spawned in.
Not even the vivisectionists of Bancroft Peak can produce such things. How is it done? I must know.

Well, I've just seen something that you lot all missed.
Atticus picks up a smoking pipe from the blackened flags.
Must be old man Alfred's... Only saw it because of the ghastly light that spire is casting.
And I could do with a quiet smoke right now too.

Another delivery. And this time it seems to be from our mysterious friend, V.
Astor cradles the container warily.
Despite my distrust of this individual, their contributions to our cause have always been useful...

A Divining Ring! The provost at Bleakhurst claimed to have seen one of these in his youth.
Vitali lays the ring on an open page to study it further.
It holds guiding magic that drains the user's vitality in order to detect hidden items.

I'm increasingly concerned about this mysterious benefactor, V.
How can we be sure that their intentions are honourable? They seem to have a thorough knowledge of both the Seekers and their power.
Perhaps they are trying to mislead us.

I am unsure... they seem to hate the Communion as much as I do and they've clearly fallen out with them at some time in the past.
I say we take whatever help we can get... And some of these relics might fetch a decent price once this nightmare is over.

Now it is complete, it is clear that this talisman is a powerful focus. A 'Thought Condenser', possibly part of the Vatalian treasury!
It allows the user to resolve separate mental and physical influences into a single empowered state of focus.
No wonder our mysterious friend was insistent that we find it.

Yet another occult tool, but I will consent to its use if it can help us with our mission.
After we are done it would be best destroyed along with the rest of the Seekers hoard!

As the twisted spire collapses, the ground begins to tremble.
You have overstepped this time, fleshlings. The tethers are cut, the fabric ripped!
This estate is but one of our anchors in your world! Your childish attempt to injure us puts your own foundations in danger.

Ah, so we can hurt you!
Astor braces herself against a doorway as the earth continues to rumble.
Your foul tendrils should not be in our world at all, and our companions should not be in yours.

Gideon may have stumbled at your gates, but I am no weak-minded novice!
Vitali brandishes his book like a warrant, his knuckles white.
We are nearing the seat of your authority, and I will have the seals needed to make my case. I demand yours now, maker! You are compelled to offer it.

I see your path little man, the same lost wandering that leads all your kind to despair and emptiness.
The Lantern tosses a medallion to the trembling ground
Take the seal, you will be interred in the rubble of this place before you gain an audience with The End.

Is everyone unharmed? That tremor was no vision! I expect the disturbance could even be felt in Blacksands.
Astor brushes dust from her arms.
The manor is well built, but I am sure I heard the rumble of collapsing masonry. We should assess the damage and decide our next steps.

Atticus laughs grimly.
These grand houses are not as firm as they appear to be. Building your mansion atop a cliff riddled with caves ain't too bright!
I'll wager this collapse will bring even more buried horrors to light.

Can you smell the stench too? The quake has caused the very ground to split and the earth below seems rotten and blighted.
Caligar nudges a pile of wreckage with her boot.
We should tread carefully to avoid both injury and infection.

I knew it would happen soon enough... Such clouds of contagion were bound to infect us at some point.
Caligar searches through her medical bag.
Unfortunately, I have no remedy in my supplies. But we can concoct a solution here. I saw a glint of 'Polmer's Algae' in the well. If we could collect a bucketful we could boil it up into a cure!

This confirms that the Ackerons were not the first owners of Highrook to open their minds to Nibiru.
Ms Voltok was seeking artistic inspiration instead of power, but she stumbled upon her own method of illumination. This moonfly extract, or at least the recordings that resulted from it, could help us assemble the final rite.

Again it is the appliance of mecanist engineering that allows us to examine her steps.
Astor wears a smug grin.
Scientific recording and containment is the only safe way to deal with arcane phenomenon. Your blind enthusiasm for occult systems is misguided and dangerous.

My 'enthusiasm' is how we have progressed this far!
Vitali curbs a rising anger
If we had not engaged with the tools and rites of Nibiru we would still be scouring the courtyard for notes and footprints!

So this is the goblet that Irma used to drink her 'vision' extract. A little theatrical, but perhaps there is something to be said for setting the scene.
Caligar's hands fidget nervously.
As a student of both the body and the mind I am interested in the effects of Voltok's experiments. Perhaps we could recreate them?

I'm all up for a good drinking session, but this seems unsafe.
Atticus shuffles nervously.
I wouldn't want you to endanger yourself, Ms Caligar. We need your expertise and sensitivity.

That is kind of you Atticus, but I am - unfortunately - a veteran of such experiments.
I feel certain that I will be fine.

The Burning Moon! The call to the innermost circle of Nibiru...
Vitali stares into the distance with a reverent gaze, his mouth curled into a smile.
This is it. An audience with the End itself! And the moment of truth. Truly, a time for enlightenment.

This is not your personal quest for revelation, Vitali! It is simply a means to an end.
Astor is visibly shaking.
Cast aside your own obsessions. We need to finish our work and return those that have been stolen! We will close this breach.

We are all under great strain. The hysteria of the situation is affecting us all in our own way.
Caligar looks to each of her colleagues in turn.
Now is not the time to stumble or to break ranks!

Aye, Ms Caligar, we can wrestle with our disagreements later. The longer this goes on, the more our minds are run ragged.
Atticus pats his club with his free hand
Let's just get this over with.

A dark melody summons me... an aspirant requests an audience?
The demon's image distorts as if it were deep underwater.
I am the arbiter of the Burning Moon. I shall await your tribute and your plea. Be wiser than your predecessor.
The Scales casts a card to the ground.

You are in-between now. The path forward lies within you.
The entity begins to slither into strands of fading gold.
I will begin the last song. It will require all of your voices, and the inner words you do not wish to speak. When it is done I shall return to hear your petition.

What has happened? The world is unravelling!
Caligar clutches at her mask, almost dragging it from her face.
The ground seethes, everything shifts like a sea mist. The splintered boards of Highrook are mixed with the dark sands of Nibiru!

It is a rapture! The veils are thinning. We are still in Highrook, but the burning moon shines down upon us!
Vitali holds his hands together, almost in prayer.
It is here, where the worlds meet, that we will triumph!

You've gone mad Vitali! As lost as that fool Ackeron!
Atticus shakes Vitali by the shoulders... he blinks and staggers.
Have you brought that cursed isle into our world, or are we now within theirs?

I see nothing but swirling fog through the windows and ghostly ground beneath.
Astor frantically rubs at her goggles.
Is Blacksands still there? And what does this new demon want of us?

Forgive my feverish outburst... the last ritual brought us to a point between worlds, we are still on our earth, but Nibiru is also here like an after-image or a shadow
Vitali stares at his companions, his face alight.
We needed to do this, to thin the veils. It is only within such proximity that we can achieve our goal!

Another path? So that is how Gideon entered Nibiru without breaching the circles!
Vitali carefully collects the key beside the note.
We must obtain this relic, it is clearly of significant power and could offer us more leverage in our dealings with the Scales.

Bookish coward... Running from his own shadow!
Atticus surveys the scene around him. His usual confidence is clearly shaken.
However - as much as I despise him - it has become hard to tell what is real and what is madness.

Yes, we are on the edge of chaos. But even as the stain of Nibiru taints our world, we must keep our minds tethered!
Astor grips the door handle as if to seize onto the solid and actual.
The only thing that sets us apart from Gideon is an adherence to sense and reality!

A pigeon? A carrier too! Arriving here in the midst of such confusion... strange, brave bird.
Atticus attempts to pick up the bird but it scuttles away from him nervously.
And there's a capsule on its leg, someone is trying to contact us...

Who would be sending us a missive now? And why use this bird?
Caligar has more luck in approaching the pigeon.
I think I might be able to sedate the poor thing in the lab, perhaps then we can get a better look at whatever it has brought to us.

What is this? Another cursed object? Another step further into the dark?
Atticus looks at the ring in disgust.
I thought we were done. That this was the last circle, the last rite, the last demon... and now what?

We are finished... The Scales has given us the means we need to conclude this sad tale...
Vitali collects the ring, twisting it around in his fingers, the light of the burning moon glitters from its surface.
We can use this, with a seal, to free one of Nibiru's prisoners... But there are four such candidates, and only three seals.

A choice that no one should have to make, but one that I somehow face daily... Which cut is the kindest?
The boy should return, he was the first victim. And the child needs his mother and father. A misguided, foolish father, but one who is clearly repentant. Perhaps he can make amends?

What?! How can you be so cruel, Doctor!
Atticus stares in dismay at Caligar.
Amy has already lost so much... And none of it of her own doing... Is she is to be cast aside simply because she is a servant?

Amy has more right to rescue than Lord Ackeron! He has done nothing but bring ruin to his family.
The mecanist pushes the air aside in a dismissive gesture.
Sophia has braved nightmare and turmoil to rescue her son... They should both be returned... Leave Gideon to rot in the nightmare he created!

But without him the boy will be robbed of a father!
Vitali places his book down and addresses his companions earnestly.
Gideon's knowledge and testimony will be part of his redemption. With his story and research recorded at Bleakhurst we can prevent this this tragedy from ever happening again.

The song is complete, though it has taken its toll on us all.
Vitali seems crestfallen, drained of his usual fervour.
We should take this to Simons Room while the notes are still fresh in our minds.. The final audience awaits.

It is done.
The Scales shimmers in impossible ways.
The song is sung, you have endured. Nibiru offers its reward.
A golden ring drops to the floor, its chime echoes through the house

There are no more words, there are no more vows.
You have the seals you have won. Use them well, when they are gone we shall become unseen once more.
The Scales dissipates, becoming one with the luminescence of the half-world.

But wait! What does that mean?
Astor is shaking, tears behind her goggles.
You must free us, free Sophia, Simon!

It is gone... We are left to make the final choice ourselves!
Vitali bows his head, his face almost blank.
And as I feared, not enough remains for all...

Like a hand on my shoulder. I can feel someone guiding me home.
Sophia turns and smiles into the distance.
Someone who cared for me once, before all this nightmare... and is that Simon I can hear?
Thank you, out there, you will always be in my heart.

The sun is rising, it feels warm.
A golden light shines on Simons face from somewhere between worlds.
I can see the gates and the garden. I can hear Mumma's machines whirring. Can I really go back? Can I?

I hope the fire is lit and Tubbs is curled up there.
I hope Pa isn't upset anymore, and Mumma is smiling, and we can all sit in the courtyard and listen to the birds again.

I can hear someone calling my name, from back in the real world?
Amy picks up her skirts and turns.
Maybe it's the old man! But, no, he is gone... could it be the voice of my dear old mum? Maybe it is time for me to go back to Blacksands, talk to my aunties, find out who I really am...
Whoever you are, thank you..

A hand of forgiveness? I will accept, though I do not deserve it.
Gideon bows his head solemnly.
I only hope that I might be able to atone somehow, and that my family will permit me some degree of redemption.
Your skills have outshone us all... thank you.

We can make no more requests of Nibiru. We have used all our tokens of recognition. What is done is done now.
Vitali looks sorrowful, yet relieved.
Thank you, my friends, for countering my over-eager mind... And now just one more ritual. A chant to close the breach.

And not a moment too soon! I fear that our party is on the brink of collapse, both mental and physical.
Caligar nods slowly.
Yes, we will all need some rest and recuperation after our return.

Aye, I've got some business to attend to, but after that I might sink a few pints in the Lobster & Pot.
Atticus pauses, and clears his throat.
Perhaps you'd like to join me good Doctor?

Unlike you I will have no time for frivolity. I must write up the report on this incident for the Venatus archives!
Astor takes a step back, hands on her hips.
And then I need to take some time to attend to a few things I've avoided for too long.

In The First Circle Of Nibiru lurks the worm. Upon the dark rot of Nibiru vegetations coil rampant, die, and grow again. Beneath that black smothering in the depthless dirt beyond sight, the worm is always burrowing, always gnawing.
It is the worm that pulses through The First Circle, the white flesh of the worm that governs the cycle of decay and feverish recombination. The ceaseless mouth of the worm is vast and pink in the black rot and we must not allow it to consume our hopes, lest it drag us into that intestinal burrow, a hell from which not even light might attempt to rescue itself.

In the Second Circle those who know not how to leave wander helpless in the Labyrinth. The faded halls echo with those who can no longer see, and who can no longer find their way. It is in this place that the power of The Cup, The Mirror, and The Song are most keenly felt. Each of these timeless entities knits derangement upon the souls they toy with in this cursed place. These prisoners come to believe there is no way out of the Labyrinth, and that soon that the minotaur will find them.
But there is a way out, and it is always through the gate of our own faith.

In the Third Circle of Nibiru one must not look up from the ashen paths. Those who let their gaze rise inadvertant and uncontrolled will glimpse those who lurk in the obsidian spires. The creatures in the spires cannot leave and have never left, for their wombs and prisons are the jagged black towers. They are vampires, feeding on the despair which falls like snow through the circles of Nibiru. It is said that a crack is forming in the spires, and that come the day of the rendering their inhabitants will be freed.
Do not look upon the Obsidian Spires, travellers in Nibiru, for to lock eyes with their inhabitants is to make the day of rendering come sooner. And they are waiting.

In the Fourth Circle of Nibiru the black desert rolls endless and poisoned. The dead lakes of this horizon burn with static. To pass into this underworld is to feel the tremors of the alien curse which sits beneath the universe like an abstract centipede, its fangs deep, pumping their venom across all the centuries of our plight.
To face the black desert is to be judged and to be hunted. Expect to find blood, to not know where it is the wounds appear from, and for the lacerations to travel through you like bloodied weather.
It is the realm of The Scales, The Root, and The Knife. And none shall pass in this sphere with their fate unmutilated.

Ever since the founding of Blacksands, the Eastersea trade has brought exotic tools and materials into the city. The first landfall for exploratory vessels, Blacksands gathers trinkets like ships gather barnacles.
Amongst the abundance of imports, rare arcane tools stand out to the educated eye.
A few remarkable items and devices, rich in potential, are discovered in each haul. Those with a sensitivity to the occult are drawn to these tools, perhaps sensing their uncanny provenance. They are coveted, passed on and even strengthened in secret workshops and forges.
Such objects become treasured, and provide invaluable support to those who study the hidden arts of the world.

A cluster of pale crystal shards has sprung from the floor, like a frosted flower. They fill the air with an uncanny chill that torments the mind.
We can sweep them away to somewhere less populated, or simply wait for them to melt and fade. But they will cause mental stress to anyone that shares a space with them.

The Key has returned to Nibiru, but a dark runic scar remains, etched into the floor of the chapel like a wound. A fetid draught rises from its inky outlines.
This is a tear in the world, left behind in the aftermath of a dark ritual.
Whilst present, this fracture might provide ingress to things from beyond.
To mend this fracture, we need to banish the entities it gives birth to.

A squirming herd of maggot-like grubs. They swarm across the damp rock walls, dropping on passers to bite and suck.
If we stay here while the worms are present they will harm us.

A cloud of simmering spores, a brackish yellow haze that seems to arise from everywhere and nowhere. Its sickening spores catch in the throat and cause hacking coughs which wrack the victim with painful spasms.
We might be able to filter them away somehow, or neutralise them with smoke.
An entity has crossed the veil

A carpet of fine thorny tendrils has sprouted beneath our feet. These wiry coils of bramble-like roots desperately wrap themselves around anything in reach, stifling whatever they can grasp. Moving through this field of clutching threads is exhausting, each step a miniature battle with the writhing rhizomes.
Perhaps we can melt them away, or dig out their source.
An entity has crossed the veil

A gross glistening worm, its twisting bulbous form almost knee high as it rolls across the floor, its puckered mouth drooling and flexing. A set of spiral shard teeth in its grim maw will snatch at anything living within reach.
Perhaps we can crush or bury this slavering worm..
An entity has crossed the veil

A gross glistening cocoon, its twisting bulbous form pulsates angrily. Its gelatinous skin should be soft, yet the phantom carapace is armoured like steel. It emits a constant whine, a half heard buzzing that burrows into the mind and drives the listener to distraction. Perhaps we can subdue its complaints somehow.

Those mushrooms disagreed with me. They must have been on the turn. Their ripe flesh has left a sickening scent in the air.
Either there was something mouldy in that last pipe, or I have smoked too much...
We can't currently extract anything useful from this task. We are holding all the possible inspirations it can impart. We should try again later, when such gifts have been used up.
The night has not imparted wisdom this time, but at least it was free of nightmares.

This rose tinted monocle is constructed with an exotic bulbous lens that improves the clarity of smudged or faded text. The lens itself comes from a set of polished glass discs, found in an ornate chest, washed ashore in Ashport during the great Coriolis storm a few years ago.
Once the quality of the lenses was realised, they became much sought after, exchanging hands for extortionate sums across the city. Arlow Irving, head archivist at the Venatus Institute was one of the first to commission eyewear manufactured with such lenses.
Irving directed the reconstruction of Venatus' famous, yet crumbling library. He had a hawk's eye for detail and whimsically claimed that he could read the books through their covers. But it was generally surmised that his remarkable acuity came from some magical quality imbued in the monocle itself.

How it found its way to Blacksands is a mystery, but this curious lens originated far to the east, in the land of Akkar.
It was stolen decades ago from the great statue of Oss, by Tohil - a notorious thief and gambler. It is rumoured that Tohil scaled the great effigy while drunk and prized the left eye from its ancient marble socket.
Although he accumulated an eclectic collection of goods in his career, Tohil lost his finds to debts, almost as quickly as he acquired them.
The lens had changed hands innumerable times, before it found its way to the underground markets of Direwych. But of all its owners, few have known how to activate its focusing power. It is said that only an Atlaxian spell is able to clear the cloud from its glass and allow its use as a powerful affix for lanterns and luminaries.

A classical curved lute. Its marbled wood burnished gold with age. When plucked it vibrates with a mesmeric tone.
Didcott was a minstrel of the old tradition, determined to preserve the songs and tales of older times through modern performance. His shows became fashionable events for aspiring cultural connoisseurs, who praised the hypnotic quality of his playing. Over time Didcott's fame grew and the conservatoire of Hindberg offered him a residency.
Unfortunately Didcott was waylaid when travelling to the appointment, and his lyre was stolen. Despite being gifted instruments by some of the finest craftsman on the winter coast, his star faded, he sank into obscurity and rarely sang again in public.

A relic of the past lives that were lived in this place. What was it that was picked from the garden and placed in this rustic carry-all? Whatever it was, it has left its traces, both physical and psychic. A rich pigment, and an echo. There is a name burned carefully into the handle. Violet. Did she care for the garden? Did she watch things grow and then wither, as all things must?
Perhaps this will lead to other discoveries left over from the shadowed past. It seems certain that it will.

A graceful vessel, composed of elegant curves and forged from prismatic crystal.
Jonathan Moxton was a vitner of some repute. One of the few winemakers to succeed in cultivating grapes on the cold east coast. Decadent tasting sessions at his clifftop plantation became popular with the city elite - who invariably made bulk orders before leaving.
However, many spoke of how the wine seemed to lose its bouquet when sampled at home. Some said that it didn't travel well, but others claimed the difference was due to the strange decanter Moxton used to serve his guests.
And indeed, when this unusual glassware vanished some years ago, Moxton's business suffered a terminal decline. His empty plantation still clings in ruined tiers to the chalky cliffs of Solstice Reach.

A ragged cloth donkey, threadbare and thin. Its lack of stuffing makes it almost two dimensional, but despite its ruinous condition, the donkey spirit still burns bright in this studded toy. Close contact with the thing reminds a person of their childhood. Glimpses of forgotten days in the playrooms of infancy, when all was new and enchanted.
Stoical and solid, the beast is always there to lighten the load and calm the nerves with its doleful eyes and patient manner.

The runes around this kintsugi-repaired pot seem to glow faintly, like glyphs traced in ember.
Indika Unmat was a respected herbalist, known for her exotic - and sometimes unorthodox - dishes. She claimed that the culinary benefits of this urn derived from the expert selection of spices she kept within it.
Her competitors were less generous, asserting that any 'special' flavouring came from the mysterious metal that held the shards together.

Arthur Kittle was an eminent research fellow at the Caincross Sanitarium. His specialism lay in the study of microscopic homunculi, entirely fictional parasitic beings that he claimed were the source of many obscure maladies. Convinced that such tiny creatures were causing havoc inside the minds of the insane, Kittle commissioned the most accurate microscope that the east coast had ever seen.
Shipped from Ikrit, the ornate microscope contained focusing lenses of an almost astronomical quality. For years Kittle hunted his quarry with the device, plundering brains from the sanitarium mortuary.
Needless to say he found nothing, but drew the conclusion that he himself was infected and the homunculi had altered his own vision so as to render themselves invisible to his eyes, even with the aid of his miraculous microscope.

A small hand cranked generator designed to offer power for mecanist devices. Its portable and re-useable nature makes it a favourite support tool for the travelling engineer.
Azaar Javid was a nomadic automaton designer. His lifestyle made it difficult to practice his trade, and his caravan was notorious for its mechanical appearance, sprouting antennae and coughing out fumes.
More a workshop than a home, Azaar shared this wagon with an endless parade of half-built mechanical dolls. He designed his generator based on 'ritualistic energies' drawn from a strange repetitive winding action. His design was eschewed by some as 'psychically unwise' but its portability soon made it a popular addition to mecanist toolkits.

A small pendant composed of a simple brass clasp holding an eerie blood-red crystal. The interior of the tear seems to glow with liquid illumination, as if it holds a strange boiling mist.
The tear was recovered from a Valhasian burial site and brought to Blacksands during the Veldt war. It is said that it can provide the wearer with power and insight, but will extract a toll on the users' body in return.
Items of occult power such as this might be enhanced given the right location and offerings.

This is no ordinary quill. Its nib and body are encased in a series of metallic clasps and plates. Not only do these enhancements ensure that the ink does not clog, they also provide delicate slide rules and calculation references for the researcher.
Palatino Garamond was a fanatical code-breaker whose skills brought her to fame during the short-lived Panoptican War. She often attributed her success to this pen, a unique item that she claimed to have discovered in the house clearance of a deceased pagan scribe.

Jerward Evelyn was a servant to the director of 'Westfold Frontiers', a prospecting group established by Lord Mithers. The company operated for several years in the gold fields of the west coast. Its expert geologists and surveyors found little to no riches, and ended up wasting their remaining funds on gin and opium.
During this period Jerward Evelyn took care of general domestics and quietly studied his superiors. After the company collapsed he remained on the coast and found fame as a solo dredger, able to find nuggets in the most unlikely streams and silts.
He put his success down to a modified clothes strainer that he had adapted during his service to Lord Mithers. The design became famous and is now used worldwide where ever washing or indeed prospecting is done.

A delicate magnetic needle balanced in a sturdy metal case. This expertly constructed compass can help guide even the most clueless explorer.
Agatha Gillcrest was a respected explorer and zoologist, the head of acquisitions at Blacksands menagerie. She obtained this compass during the dangerous excavation of a gnostic laboratory in the Knoss Isles. Though her work meant she was rarely at her post, when she did return her expedition presentations were both erudite and hazardous.
Gillcrest was eventually fired from her post after she accidentally released a flock of formic bats into the park. Unfortunate bystanders were showered with a fine acid rain drizzle, sprayed by the escaping creatures.

A mecanist detector capable of identifying the presence of ether-waves. Its delicate needle quivers at the the unveiling of a hitherto hidden world.
The culmination of Astor’s tenacity and Lady Ackeron’s brilliance. From this a mecanist legacy can be forged.

A stately corvid, with dark beady eyes and ebony plumage. Mr Stokes preens and poses, hopping from one foot the the other like a nervous child. His midnight feathers glint like metal.
Stokes appears at random, hoping for a treat. He will even suffer to be carried, for a while at least.

A rite of returning. A chant to seal the gates of Nibiru behind.
Draw a square within a square, twisted to form an octagram.
At each vertex scribe the compass heading, and within the centre spread a mound of fresh earth into a flattened bed.
With finger lines in soil, mark the Four Circles of Nibiru.
Walk the points in an outer circle path, reciting the Coda of Valhassa at each compass point.
Lie upon the earth and sleep, counting the stars of the Burning Moon.

A rite to break the threshold of The First Circle. A knock on the gates of Nibiru.
Draw an arched door upon the wall in white chalk. Circumscribe the form in a circle and at the apex of the arch draw a twelve-point star.
With your forehead pressed against the star, sing the song of the Autumn Key.
Hold the edges of the frame, stare beyond the wall, eyes wide, until the tears drop to the floor.
Close your eyes, close your mind and open the door.

A rite to break the threshold of The Second Circle. A tribute to call upon the dreaming ruins of Nibiru.
A drunken circle drawn on the floor, its line uncertain as if seen through water.
A goblet inscribed therein and four points around the ring, compass cardinals - marked with simple vessels of wood.
Make an offering to each container - north with spittle, east with tears, south with dust, west with ash.
Sit within this constellation, eyes closed, a handful of thorns in each palm. Sing the Song of the Red Night... strike the earth with your fists until they bleed and the ground opens up.

A rite to break the threshold of The Third Circle. A ceremony to walk in the cinder fields of Nibiru.
A hexagon and a hammer contained, drawn in charcoal on the ground.
Strike a stone with metal to ring out a beckoning call. Repeat the chime, like a tolling bell, like a heart beat. Breathe in step to the clock, lungs like bellows - fanning an unseen flame.
Etch the secret names of the makers inside the hex. Draw their tools to your minds eye, until they flicker in flame like the blacksmiths hammer.
Strike the sigil with your palm, strike again, again until your bones ache and the world cracks.

A rite to break the threshold of The Fourth Circle. An artery to the heart of Nibiru.
The Eye, the Chalice, The Hammer. Mark their rings, like ripples in the still pond of time. And in the centre, a final circle, bitten at the edge, a waxing moon
Scribe its influence in scored lines of light, in curves of sacred geometry. An atomic astrolabe, its extents piercing between worlds.
Stand on the moon, face its offspring, call their names in turn. The children of the perihelion, the nomads of the aphelion... call them out.
Turn with the orbits, spin in the dervish of celestial motion. Address the terminus of every line, again and again until the world becomes dark.
A flickering form, a sense of frozen fear. Something is here and also not here. Its half-presence sends shivers through the air.
Twisting threads of smoke rise from cracks in the ground like tendrils of dark blood. A choking miasma full of fetid whispers, like an exhalation of the dead.

A Seal of Nibiru. A runic mark etched into a smooth pebble of basalt. This dark medallion is a symbol of power, a token of acknowledgement from beyond.

It will not leave of its own accord and must be driven out by force.

A shadow of a child is here, sometimes. His presence flickers like a candle.

A ghostly vision of Simon appears. In the blurring of the worlds it is neither here nor there.
These visions can be encouraged to move, as if sleepwalking, but they fade in and out like a waxing moon.

Soft wings swim in the dust of the archives. Flickering shadows fall across the shelves as moths dance around the lanterns. A fluttering typography that hints at half remembered stories.
A vision that lingers, offering a source of inspiration.

A lesser vision, through the mists of the moonfly haze, an echo from the goblets previous owner. Irma Voltok's pale hand scratches a series of archive codes on a slip of vellum.
We draw them out from the dream. Any guidance to the archives convoluted storage is a welcome addition to our endeavour.

A condensation of intention and insight, a boon resulting from the combination of focus and concentration.

A portly barrel of soft grey fur, this cement grey cat purrs industriously as he stalks the rooms of the house.
Unperturbed by the living or the dead, he maintains an air of self-sufficiency, never mewling for food or clawing for attention - an independent gentleman.
His collar offers a name, but no provenance, and he is not referenced on any residents list. Regardless, he patrols the corridors in the manner of a landlord inspecting his domain, pausing here and there to permit the occasional scratch behind his grey velvet ears.
A flask holding the distilled luminescence of flickerfish glands. When shaken, the chemicals within provide a brief but bright illumination.

Whiskers trail on walls like hands trailing in water. Sight is only a brief part of the picture. The scent of damp stonework forms a foil for more interesting odours. The contents of crates and containers give themselves away to the sensitive nose.
A vision that lingers, offering a source of inspiration.

Coiling around my limbs like a second skin. But I am not afraid, they hiss, they caress, whispering dark secrets to me.
A vision from a dream... a source of inspiration.

Chirps, chatterings and feathers. Bright calls echo around you as a tiny form flits to and fro.

It is dark but you are not blind... Cold clods of earth tumble through your fingers. You cannot see, but you can feel, smell, anticipate the myriad forms of life huddled in the soil. A mycelium diagram unfolds like a map before you.
A vision that lingers, offering a source of inspiration.

Heavy eyelids blur your view, as if peering out from a warm winter blanket. Even the glass on the table seems leagues away. But it is soon in your hand and the heady vapours drifting from its rim calm and cosset.
There is revelation in sensation... more than leaves lie at the bottom of the cup.
A vision that lingers, offering a source of inspiration.

Darts of hot light flicker in the darkness of an ashen copse. A constellation of orange points, where each beetle burns with an industrial determination.

A thin yet pungent broth, infused with the soporific flesh of the Slumber Fish. The orphanages of Deep Spire often keep cauldrons of the stuff bubbling in their great dorm rooms. Shadowy matrons doling out bowls to guarantee a quiet night.
This sleeping aid is popular in Ashburg, where the factories churn night and day. Made from dessicated Valroot, pouches of this glittering lilac dust are sought by insomiancs and addicts alike.
Just a little alchemical something to assist with the many things that sleep can provide.

A small pouch of ground herbs and spices, imported from the bustling food markets of Akkar. At least that's what the note attached says - 'Add a pinch to add some punch!'
The hunter who has killed a boar will know that it is more than meat which the noble beasts bestows upon them. What passes between are elements of the soul. And a tasty roast.

A detailed hand-drawn sheet of chemical tables and molecular diagrams - translated from some ancient tongue.
It provides a guiding matrix for budding alchemists to lay out their calculations. This worksheet could support our activities in the laboratory.

My blood buzzes, as if my body is a hive. A busy factory filled with the countless chemical tasks of my anatomy. I am in awe of the simple alchemies of the everyday.

A scampering shadow, a half-seen furry form darts around the machine room. Tools clatter and shelves creak, but the invisible interloper is helping, not hindering. A hairy hand passes you the part you require and a chattering giggle fades into the air around you.

Mr Mouse lived in a house. Not his house, but the house of a great king. Some people don't want mice in their homes, but the king was always asleep and dreaming, so Mr Mouse was free to wander the house without fear.
Most mornings Mr Mouse would climb up the curtains and look out of the windows, gazing across the ash coloured land to the evil river beyond. He knew that the river was the place where visitors would arrive, their feet making pretty patterns in the ash-grey sand.
He wanted to visit the river, but he was afraid that he would get lost on the way. So instead of venturing outside, he would watch, and whisper.

One day Mr Mouse was watching from his window and he saw a little jollyboat being paddled along the river. Sat in the boat were the four visitors that he had been expecting.
With a squeak, Mr Mouse climbed down from the window. He knew that the visitors must never see him, or all would be lost. He was, after all, just a little mouse.
Pulling on his little mouse jacket, Mr Mouse scurried to his cosy mouse-hole in the wall. He would have to prepare for the arrivals. They were here to meddle with the great king's dreams! Perhaps they would even put some of them in jars and take them away. And Mr Mouse couldn't have that.

Mr Mouse could hear muffled voices from beyond the walls. The visitors were here. He heard them fiddling with the door, trying the doorknob, and prying at the lock with their strange tools. Eventually he heard them come inside the house.
Mr Mouse scurried along the little corridors in the walls of his home. The bootprints of the visitors wrote a message in the ash from the riverbank, but Mr Mouse could not read it. He was just a mouse. He could see the shadows of the visitors moving about in the other rooms, quietly searching. They were seeking for the Great King's dreams. They must not find them! Mr Mouse had an idea. He was going to place something irresistible in a trap.

Mr Mouse knew that the visitors were looking for the Great King's dreams. He knew where to find one! The dream was nestled in a dark corner, like a beetle hibernating for winter in the cracks of the house.
Mr Mouse dragged the dream out of its hiding place, even though it was squirming and biting. Carefully, so as not to make too much sound, Mr Mouse took the dream to The Room of The Stones, where the writing crawled like worms. There, he thought, he would place the dream as bait beneath the hidden cage. The dream lay on the floor on its back, desperately writhing.
Mr Mouse found the rope that held the cage, and with his sharp front teeth, he began to gnaw and chew.

Mr Mouse had laid a trap for the visitors! They entered the darkened room and saw the helpless dream struggling on the floor. They rushed to it, like mice to old cheese. The visitors kneeled down around the dream, with their syringes and their books. Mr Mouse gnawed faster! The rope snapped. The cage fell. The visitors screamed.
Mr Mouse hoped all the noise would not wake up the king! But up in his grand bedroom, the king slumbered on, dreaming his dreams, until they climbed out of his skull to crawl off and hide in the nooks and crannies of the house.
Mr Mouse had done a good job.
He went back to the window, to watch the river, and to whisper. And to wait.

He shuffles a pile of dead leaves over the hole and begins to retrace his footsteps back to the house, the dawn sky gaining blood behind him.

Despite the winter air, the noon sun beats down on the courtyard. The enclosing walls create a crumbling shelter from the clifftop winds. Alfred, the Ackerons' Groundskeeper is clearing brambles from around the main gates. Amy sits on the cracked stone stoop, shucking peas into a wicker trug.
'Why don't you go fetch my sickle, love?' Alfred's shoulders are hunched with age and stress, but he tries to hide his unease from his daughter. She shrugs, sets down her basket, and heads into the house.
Alfred quickly stashes something behind a loose brick in the crumbling garden wall. Satisfied with this subterfuge, he returns reluctantly to his thorny struggle.

The damp walls of the cellar glisten in the light of an approaching candle. Alfred is here, slowly descending the grimy stairs. He shifts his weight awkwardly, trying to avoid the inevitable groans of the ancient wood. Under one arm he carries a small box stacked with wax cylinders.
After Sophia presented a Phonograph device to her son, Alfred has enjoyed finding the boy any cylinders he could locate in the archives.
This particular collection however, was marked with the occult signs of the Communion, and Alfred is determined that Simon should never hear their contents. Enough damage has already been done.
He hides the crate under an thick tarpaulin and slowly retraces his steps from the undercroft.

I was in the kitchen, and Pa comes in, all clumsy and loud. He's dragging a sack of coal for the stove, and he don't see me as I'm in the pantry sorting some provisions.
He drops the bag and then takes something small and shiny from his pocket and puts it in one of the tool drawers under the sinks, the ones no one ever uses. Covers it up I reckon, because I can hear him rattling about with the other stuff in there...
When he starts stoking the fire I come out and give him a hug and don't say anything, poor old fool.

I'd been making the beds and rolling up the old linen when Pa comes in. He looks all nervous, looking over his shoulder and that, like someone is following him.
He tells me that He heard the Lady Sophia calling for me and that I need to go see her sharp. But I know he ain't all telling the truth here.
So when I leave the room I waits outside the door for a while. I can hear him stashing something in there, clanking with a noise that only the old washbowl makes. So I reckon he's stashed another of his secrets there...
I keep meaning to go back and see what it might be - I hope its not just more smokeweed - but with Simon so poorly I am spending most of my time taking care of him...

I'd been puttin away the best silver, an dustin off the glassware when i saw the old mans pipe.. on the floor, under one of the cabinets.
I goes down to get it and sees he has sprung up one of the boards, right out of sight, clearly to hide somethin' under it.
I didn't want to lever it up to see what hes stashed, but it cant be big.. I took his pipe back to him though, he was happy with that.

I don't like going down the cellars much... The top chambers are ok, but once you get further down it gets all clammy and sick feeling and there's too many doors, I don't know my way around...But I had to go down yesterday because Mr Gideon wanted some bottles of liquor.
When I gets there I see Pa shuffling around, wedging a box up on one of the beams.
'What are you up to old man?' I says cheerily.. But he replies in some dark tone 'Never you mind child, ain't none of your business'.
I felt all taken aback, but I says nothing and carry on with my chore. But I did remembered the joist though, where he put the box thing on top.
